description: Good Foods Group Launches "Guacxiety," a New Campaign About the Stress of Buying Avocados Backed by new Good Foods/Harris Poll data showing 82% of avocado purchasers get frustrated when avocados go bad before they can use them, the campaign puts a name to a stress most buyers already recognize Good Foods Group recently launched “Guacxiety,” a campaign about the nagging uncertainty of buying an avocado and not knowing whether it will be ready when you are. Created with challenger marketing consultancy Rival, the campaign runs across digital channels and connected TV and draws directly on the meme formats and comment-section discourse that have made avocado timing a running joke on social media. Rather than inventing a tension, the creative borrows the one consumers have already been posting about for years. “Guacxiety” also introduces a free, limited-edition avocado stress ball, available to order at goodfoods.com beginning September 16th while supplies last. The avocado stress ball plugs into a bigger moment, one where squishy fidget toys have become a fixture of Gen Z culture on TikTok and Instagram and squeezing something soft is an ordinary way to take the edge off a stressful day. New data suggests the online discourse around fresh avocados is grounded in a real, offline frustration. In a survey conducted online by The Harris Poll on behalf of Good Foods Group, more than 4 in 5 Americans (83%) purchase fresh avocados. Among avocado purchasers, 82% say they get frustrated when avocados go bad before they can use them and more than two in three (68%) agree that buying fresh, whole avocados often feels like a guessing game. Other findings among avocado purchasers include: ● Over three quarters (76%) agree fresh, whole avocados often go from too hard to overripe faster than expected ● 69% say getting the timing right when buying fresh, whole avocados feels like a matter of luck. ● Two in three (67%) worry the avocados they buy will not be ripe when they need them "The number that stopped us was 82%. Four out of five people who buy avocados have watched one go bad before they got to use it. That is not a small annoyance, it is a repeated one, and it is why so much of the conversation online is people joking about something that genuinely bothers them," said Mandy Bottomlee, Director of Content Marketing at Good Foods Group. "That is exactly the anxiety we take off the table at Good Foods Group. We make fresh, craveable guacamole that is ready when you open it, so nobody is left guessing.” "The tension around avocados is real, just look at the running jokes across social media,” said Mikayla Belson, Creative Director at Rival. “So when the idea of the Guacxiety Stress Ball came up, we immediately wanted to make that real, too. In our eyes, it’s the opposite of a hard sell. And that’s the spirit of the whole campaign. From the videos, to the website, to the stress balls, it’s all just a fun, light-hearted break in your day, which is a perfect fit for a brand like Good Foods.” Good Foods makes ready-to-eat guacamole using high-pressure processing, a cold technique that preserves texture and flavor without heat. The company's products are sold at grocery stores and warehouse clubs nationwide including Costco, Kroger, Target and Publix. description: With Meta Connect kicking off this week in Menlo Park and concerns around privacy and consent continuing to grow, Even Realities, the consumer technology company behind camera-free, display-first smart glasses, is launching “Exposed,” a new campaign exploring what happens to bystanders when cameras move from our phones onto our faces. Created in partnership with VIRTUE Worldwide, part of VICE Media, “Exposed” is rolling out across New York and the San Francisco Bay Area this week, ahead of an eight-episode cinematic micro-drama directed by Ishana Night Shyamalan and launching on TikTok on October 8. “Exposed” is built around a simple premise: smart glasses do not need cameras to be useful, and as wearable technology becomes more prevalent, the industry must consider not only the people wearing these devices, but also everyone around them. In New York, “Exposed” has taken over Times Square, with additional placements forthcoming in gyms and bathrooms across Manhattan, bringing the message into spaces where people may least expect to be filmed without their knowledge or consent. In San Francisco and Silicon Valley, the campaign is rolling out across the region, including on a wrapped bus running around Meta’s campus throughout Meta Connect this week before continuing through some of the Bay Area’s biggest technology hubs. “We didn’t want to run another traditional ad that people instantly skip; we wanted to, as always, tap into a cultural conversation and build a piece of entertainment genuinely worth watching,” said Deepa Patel, Managing Director at VIRTUE Worldwide. “As public fatigue around surveillance and unconsenting recording reaches a huge boiling point, cinematic, suspense-driven storytelling is the only way to make people not only see but truly feel the stakes of losing their privacy. Partnering with Even Realities for their US debut has been an incredible journey, and we’re immensely proud to be their trusted partner to help them introduce camera-free smart glasses to American consumers and redefine what human connection and true privacy really look like.” On October 8, “Exposed” will expand into an eight-episode cinematic micro-drama, bringing the campaign’s themes of privacy and consent to life through a suspense story built for social. The teaser is available now on TikTok and Instagram, with the full series launching on TikTok at @evenrealities. More About “Exposed”: About The Creative Concept: When Even Realities and VIRTUE began exploring a future in which face-worn cameras become increasingly commonplace, the idea naturally lent itself to suspense. Unlike a phone, which typically needs to be taken out and pointed at something to record, camera-enabled eyewear can make it less apparent when recording is taking place. Rather than building a traditional product campaign around features or specifications, “Exposed” explores that tension through entertainment. With Ishana Night Shyamalan directing, the campaign uses cinematic storytelling to show how everyday interactions change when people are unsure whether they are being recorded. The series deliberately avoids traditional product placement and feature demonstrations. Instead, the connection to Even Realities comes through the campaign’s central idea: smart eyewear can take a different approach, and cameras don't have to be part of it. About the Strategy: “Exposed” arrives as camera-enabled smart glasses become increasingly visible in everyday life, raising new questions about bystander privacy and consent in public and private spaces. The campaign brings those questions directly into environments where the tension is especially tangible, from gyms and bathrooms in Manhattan to Times Square and the area surrounding Meta’s campus during Meta Connect. Through its out-of-home activations and upcoming social series, “Exposed” invites people to consider how wearable cameras could change expectations around when, where, and how people are recorded. Even Realities takes a different approach to smart eyewear. Its Even G2 smart glasses are designed without a camera, instead using a display-first experience to provide information including navigation, live translation, notifications, and teleprompting directly within the wearer’s field of view. This  professional campaign titled 'Exposed' was published in United States in September, 2026. It was created for the brand: Even Realities, by ad agencies: VICE Media and VIRTUE Worldwide. description: Dentsu Creative has launched ‘Primetime Play’, a new long-term brand platform and visual identity for Sky Vegas, designed to reconnect the brand with Sky’s heritage as one of the UK’s leading entertainment brands. Rooted in entertainment, the platform turns everyday moments of downtime into moments of ‘Primetime Play’, creating a distinctive brand world designed to stretch far beyond advertising into product, proposition and customer experience. The launch film is fronted by Kaya Scodelario, fresh from filming the second season of Netflix’s The Gentlemen, and directed by Scott Lyon through Rogue. Set to Mark Ronson’s Ooh Wee, the film sees Scodelario move through an immersive Sky Vegas studio, with each window revealing a different game-inspired world. Volcanic landscapes erupt, diamond vaults burst open, tropical rainforests come alive and a giant kraken emerges from the deep. Combining in-camera production with VFX from Electric Theatre Collective, the film brings together spectacle, imagination and a sense of playful escapism. The platform launches across TV, VOD, social, radio, digital audio, sponsorship idents, digital display, CRM and owned channels, with media handled by EssenceMediacom. A major national OOH rollout includes a Waterloo Gallery takeover featuring bespoke 3D special builds, while a new suite of sponsorship idents introduces recurring characters from within the Sky Vegas studio. More than a single campaign, Primetime Play has been created as a flexible, transformational platform that will shape how Sky Vegas looks, feels and behaves into 2027 and beyond, with refreshed website and app experiences launching alongside the work and further developments planned as the platform evolves. video_title: London Philharmonic Orchestra — The Power of Listening
description: The London Philharmonic Orchestra today announces the adoption of its new brand platform, “The Power of Listening”, created by Ace of Hearts. “The Power of Listening” is the new long-term vision for the London Philharmonic Orchestra, with Jesús Herrera heading up his first full season as Artistic Director. “The Power of Listening” is a manifestation of the principle at the London Philharmonic Orchestra’s core; the shared exchange between musicians, audiences and communities that creates connection, emotion and collective human experience. This vision will be embedded in the way the Orchestra approaches artistic programming, future collaborations, its education and community work, and its public communications going forward. The first piece of communications built on this bold new vision, in collaboration with the Royal College of Art, launches today. It is an invitation to stop and truly listen - for audiences who already know the Orchestra and those who don’t yet. Jesús Herrera, Artistic Director of the London Philharmonic Orchestra said: "Listening is often thought of as something we do passively, but music can have a profound effect on how we feel and what we imagine. By bringing together the London Philharmonic Orchestra and the Royal College of Art, we wanted to make that invisible experience visible - and show people that you don't need to be an expert in classical music to have a powerful response to it." David Burke, Chief Executive of the London Philharmonic Orchestra commented, “The Power of Listening is a statement about the kind of Orchestra we are: open, connected to the culture around us and relevant both to those who already know us and those who might never have set foot in a concert hall. It’s a long-term commitment to opening up what orchestral music can offer and who it can be for. If our music moves you on a London street, we hope you’ll come and hear it played live.” The first piece of work under this new brand platform is a series of original artworks, created by Royal College of Art postgraduate artists. Mentored by Neville Brody OBE, Professor of Communications at the Royal College of Art, the artists were each asked to listen to a piece of music, with a single instruction to make something out of the feelings it evokes. The music pieces came from the Orchestra's own record label, encapsulating six decades of the Orchestra’s history under five of its Principal Conductors, past and present. These artworks represent completely different accounts of the power of listening, highlighting the contrasting ways music affects us. A specially built “Listening Wall” installation brings each artwork to life. All eight of the designs have been paired with a set of headphones, inviting passers-by at Vinegar Yard, London SE1, to listen to the very piece of music that inspired each artwork, allowing them to experience the power of deep, active listening and its ability to inspire creativity and emotion. The installation is designed to reach people who may never have considered an orchestral experience as being “for them”. The campaign extends across paid and organic social and (D)OOH across London, led by a hero film capturing the exploration of the power of listening in collaboration with RCA. The film was directed by Talia Beale, who is represented by Academy Films, and co-produced by Academy Films and Ace of Hearts. Talia is a multifunctional artist, musician and filmmaker who has previously worked with Jonathan Glazer on his Warchild project. Rasmus Smith Bech, Executive Creative Director and Partner at creative company Ace of Hearts commented, “It’s been an absolute privilege to collaborate with an institution such as the London Philharmonic Orchestra and help define and sharpen their future mission. We came in to give them a way of showing the world what is already at the core of their brand. ‘The Power of Listening’ is that idea, and it has turned out to travel much further than the advertising. Working with Neville Brody and a group of up and coming artists from the Royal College of Art on the first expression of it, with Jesús Herrera carrying it through the organisation, is the best start we could have asked for." Neville Brody OBE, Professor of Communication at the Royal College of Art said: “Translating a symphony into a still image is a near-impossible task. In a moment when images can be generated in seconds by a machine, there’s something urgent about asking a person to sit, listen and really feel something before they make a mark. Through this partnership with the London Philharmonic Orchestra and the Royal College of Art, eight artists were asked to do exactly that: listen deeply to orchestral music and turn what they heard and felt into something visual.” This  professional campaign titled 'The Power of Listening' was published in United Kingdom in September, 2026. It was created for the brand: London Philharmonic Orchestra, by ad agency: Ace of Hearts. description: Carvana just dropped the next chapter of its Shaq partnership, and this one puts him to work in an unexpected place. Let's just say the views are great, but he's not exactly what customers ordered. The campaign was created by Carvana, produced by Good Behavior and directed by Win Bates. This new spot builds on the brand’s "Shaqvana" campaign from last fall. The partnership itself originally grew out of Shaq's own long-running fascination with Carvana's car vending machines, so this next chapter felt like a natural evolution. "Shaq doesn't do anything small, so of course his next move was setting up shop in one of our largest vending machines," said Ryan Keeton, Carvana Co-Founder and Chief Brand Officer. "This spot marks the next chapter of our partnership with him, and we're excited to keep finding new ways to bring his big personality to life." “Shaq was hilarious and surprisingly not that tall,” said Bates. He shook my hand and said ‘If the commercial is good, it’s me. And if it’s bad, it’s you.’ I really hope I did not let him down.” This  professional campaign titled 'The Big Diesel Has a New Office' was published in United States in September, 2026. video_title: Upward — Match Group bets on the return of modern courtship.
description: Upward is ushering in a new era of dating as the home of modern courtship, welcoming a broader generation who know marriage is the goal and believe the way they date should reflect it. Match Group’s 2026 Singles in America study points to a generational shift: 72% of Gen Z want to get married, more than any other generation. Upward gives that ambition a home through modern courtship, putting marriage at the center of dating with clear intentions, purposeful pursuit and mutual effort from the start. Launched in 2020, Upward was built from a community that had strong conviction around faith, family and marriage. The relaunch builds on that foundation to welcome a broader generation reclaiming traditional courtship for modern life, where wanting a family is an ambition to embrace, not something to downplay. “For a generation told to keep things casual and see where they go, saying you want marriage can almost feel countercultural,” said Lauren DeFord, Director of Brand Marketing at Match Group. “Upward members have always been clear about what they’re building toward. Built for people dating with marriage in mind, Upward is a home for singles who know what they want, hold strong standards and believe dating should lead somewhere.” Match Group research points to the size of that opportunity. Approximately one in four U.S. singles ages 18–34 strongly identifies with a combination of traditional values around family, faith and community while navigating modern life. The relaunch brings modern courtship to life through a refreshed app experience designed to make values, future goals and relationship expectations more visible earlier in dating. Chivalry Mode is an opt-in experience for members who prefer a more traditional first-move dynamic. When both members opt in, he is encouraged to send the first message and she chooses whether to respond or politely unmatch. Marriage Timeline lets members share when they hope to get married and see whether potential matches share a similar timeline. Core Values gives members a way to show what matters most to them and quickly see whether they share a potential match’s priorities. This is modern courtship in action: women are clear about their standards, men pursue with purpose, and both move toward marriage together. The clearest proof of Upward’s purpose is why members join and why they leave. Nearly every Upward member ages 18–30 surveyed says they want a family, making “family” the platform’s most-selected Core Value. And the #1 reason members say they leave is the outcome Upward is built for: they found someone worth leaving the app for. The relaunch also introduces a new visual identity created in partnership with Corner Table Creative. A refined logo and app icon, distinctive typography and romantic imagery give Upward a bolder, more confident expression of its marriage-minded purpose. Drawing from Americana and the intimacy of a personal scrapbook, the new identity feels warm, nostalgic and distinctly human, anchored by subtle ring-inspired detail. The accompanying “Wanted for Life” campaign brings that purpose to life through a playful, modern take on wanted posters. It celebrates the qualities members want in a lifelong partner, from good manners and meaningful effort to commitment that goes the distance. Through playful lines like “Known to change a tire, not his feelings for you” and “Often described as wifey material,” Upward puts commitment and courtship where its members believe they belong: at the center of dating, not in a conversation saved for later. “We wanted Upward’s new brand to feel as intentional as the people who use it,” said Rachel Brandt, CEO of Corner Table Creative. “By pairing the intimacy of a scrapbook with the boldness of Americana and wanted posters, we made the pursuit of lasting love feel confident, human, and a little rebellious.” The campaign will roll out across paid and organic social, streaming video and audio ads, with additional creative featuring real Upward couples who found lasting love on the app, bringing modern courtship to life from first match to marriage. video_title: King's Hawaiian — Best Slider in Football
description: Off the field, King’s Hawaiian has perfected the slider, made on their irresistible rolls. On the field, Eli Manning perfected the quarterback slide. Now, the two are bringing their respective expertise together to call on football to recognize one of football’s most overlooked moves: the quarterback slide. For generations, King’s Hawaiian has been the bread behind some of gameday’s best sliders, from buffalo chicken to pulled pork to chopped cheese. Meanwhile, throughout his legendary career, Manning made a name for himself by knowing exactly when to throw, when to run and when to slide. Together, in the brand’s latest campaign, “The Best Slider in Football,” King’s Hawaiian and Manning agree:  while King’s Hawaiian makes the best sliders off the field, Eli made some of the best slides on it. There’s just one problem: you can’t be the best if no one is keeping score. If you didn’t know, the quarterback slide isn’t recognized as an official statistic. For a quarterback, sliding is a strategic decision to end a play while avoiding a potentially significant hit. Knowing when to stop chasing extra yards and get down is a skill in its own right—and one that has generated plenty of debate among players, coaches, fans and media. So, if football tracks so much of what happens on the field – from passing yards to rushing yards to sacks, why doesn’t it track the slide? That’s why King’s Hawaiian and Manning are launching a petition, calling on football to recognize quarterback slides as an official statistic. Fans can join Eli by signing the petition at  www.BestSliderInFootball.com  — and those who sign and submit proof of their signature will have the chance to win** FREE King’s Hawaiian slider buns for LIFE*. Because if fans help recognize football’s best sliders on the field, King’s Hawaiian will take care of the best sliders off of it. “Sliders are a crucial part of game day, both on and off the field,” said Raouf Moussa, CMO at King’s Hawaiian. “Therefore, we want to recognize their importance by making them an official stat. We knew we had to team up with one of the most iconic quarterbacks to help right this wrong.” “The best way to settle a debate about the best slider in football is to look at the stats, so when King’s Hawaiian came up with the stroke of inspiration to track quarterback slides, I couldn’t wait to work with them to bring this to football and slider fans everywhere,” said Eli Manning. Created in partnership with creative agency Erich & Kallman, “The Best Slider in Football” campaign is also coming to screens nationwide in a new King’s Hawaiian commercial spot starring Manning. Running throughout football season, the spot brings the playful slider debate to life as Manning makes his case for the title of “Best Slider in Football” while King’s Hawaiian reminds fans who has the title locked down off the field. This  professional campaign titled 'Best Slider in Football' was published in United States in September, 2026. It was created for the brand: King's Hawaiian, by ad agency: Erich & Kallman. description: As conflict in the Middle East disrupted international travel plans, Green World Adventures—a Costa Rican destination management company—responded with an alternative rooted in a country that abolished its army in 1948. “Make Pura Vida, Not War” is a seven-piece print campaign that reinterprets the language of conflict through real Costa Rican experiences. Each execution replaces fear and uncertainty with nature, adventure and the optimism of pura vida. When the world talked about war, Costa Rica answered with life. Targeted to UK travellers reconsidering their destination choices, the campaign also helped Green World Adventures build direct demand beyond traditional travel intermediaries. video_title: Universal Orlando Resorts — Stay Near The Fear
description: Universal Orlando Resort announces the return of its highly anticipated "Stay Near The Fear" vacation packages, offering horror fans the ultimate way to experience Halloween Horror Nights 2026. Running on select nights from August 28 through November 1, 2026, this year's premier scare event features a terrifying lineup of 10 all-new haunted houses, four immersive scare zones, and two live entertainment shows. By booking an official on-property resort stay, guests can seamlessly transition from the fog-filled streets of Universal Studios Florida to the comfort of their hotel rooms without missing a single heartbeat. The centerpiece of the "Stay Near The Fear" campaign is an array of exclusive theme park perks designed to maximize survival time inside the event. On-property hotel guests unlock a dedicated event entry gate from 6:30 PM to 7:30 PM, allowing them to bypass the massive main gates and plunge straight into the horror. Additionally, packages offer seamless integration with Stay & Scream early access, granting daytime ticket holders entry into designated park holding zones starting at 2:00 PM to conquer select haunted houses before the general public is even admitted. This year, the terror refuses to stay behind park gates as Universal's resort hotels undergo unprecedented spooky transformations. For the 2026 season, the horror expands directly into the hotel lobbies and lounges, featuring highly detailed photo illusions and themed specialty menus. Guests staying at Loews Royal Pacific Resort will encounter an immersive Dracula takeover, while Universal's Cabana Bay Beach Resort plays host to the sinister Pumpkin Lord, and Universal Aventura Hotel delivers eerie, out-of-this-world Alien Takeover energy. To ensure a stress-free getaway, "Stay Near The Fear" packages bundle specially priced event admission, resort accommodations, and complimentary transportation into one comprehensive vacation. Guests can choose from a range of accommodation tiers — from the luxurious Premier hotels featuring free daytime Express Passes, to the budget-friendly 2-Bedroom Suites at Universal's Endless Summer Resort — all serviced by complimentary water taxis or shuttle buses running well past the event's 2:00 AM conclusion. Travel agents and guests can explore complete package details and secure bookings immediately by visiting the official Universal Orlando Resort Vacation Portal. video_title: MilkPEP — milkXP, Closing the Teen Relevance Gap
description: Today, MilkPEP launches milkXP, a new free YouTube series that pairs popular creators with educators to make real-world topics more relevant and engaging for teens. Developed in partnership with its agency of record, GALE, the series illustrates how classroom learning can help fuel real-world goals. For instance, the first semester explores financial literacy, one of the subjects teens connect most closely with their future goals. In each milkXP episode, an educator teams up with a creator to explore a topic teens want to understand through the storytelling and pacing they expect and genuinely enjoy online. Each episode is guided by the Milk Flow State Framework, a digital content scorecard developed with digital wellness expert Dr. Michael Rich and reviewed by education expert Dr. Gregory Barton. The framework is designed to help ensure that content is age-appropriate, participatory, and purposeful. The strategy of the YouTube series is directly inspired by new research findings from the new Relevance Study Gap commissioned by Milk and conducted by The Harris Poll, showing that teens may disengage when what they are learning does not feel connected to their lives or futures. 55% of teens say what they learn in school does not feel relevant to what they need for future success, and 97% say they are less engaged when they cannot connect a lesson to their goals or interests. 69% of teens use YouTube several times a week or daily to learn something new, and 95% would watch long-form YouTube educational content connecting school subjects with real-world opportunities, careers, and goals. Strategically, the content bridges classroom learning with a platform teens already use, connecting educators with creators to make education part of the content they already enjoy. Milk also fits naturally into the program: 74% of teens say they reach for a snack or drink when it's time to focus on homework, and 94% say a nutritious breakfast or lunch makes it easier to concentrate. An eight-ounce serving of dairy milk delivers 13 essential nutrients — including protein, vitamin B12, iodine, and zinc — showing how milk can fuel their focus throughout the day. The series premieres September 15 and features creator collaborations with Ben Azelart (4.7M), Lexi Rivera (8M), Harper Zilmer (1M), Angelo Bahu (1M), SeanDoesMagic (7.3M), and Markell Washington (1.3M). The latest work in the partnership continues GALE’s innovative approach to tapping into the back-to-school season, with a recent satirical campaign featuring John Morgan of the personal injury law firm Morgan & Morgan warning parents that whole milk’s healthy fats support kids’ brain development, making their brains more appetizing to zombies. The series will be showcased on YouTube @milkXPofficial and run through the fall. video_title: Hyundai — The Mark of a Warrior - Little Warriors
description: Hyundai Motor America and INNOCEAN USA have launched “The Mark of a Warrior,” a national campaign supporting Hyundai Hope on Wheels, the company’s nonprofit focused on helping end childhood cancer. Built around the organisation’s iconic handprint, the campaign transforms the symbol into an emblem of courage and resilience, presenting children fighting cancer as “Little Warriors.” The cinematic hero film, “Little Warrior,” was directed by Matthijs van Heijningen via MJZ and narrated by Scarlett Johansson in her debut as Hyundai’s new brand voice. The film follows a young girl battling a gigantic monster in a colosseum, eventually defeating it with a single decisive blow using her painted palm. The visual metaphor concludes with the child placing the handprint on her face and ringing a bell to a cheering crowd. The 60-second film launched around the opening game of the NFL season and is running nationally across broadcast, streaming, digital and social channels throughout September and beyond. The wider campaign also includes social content and community activations designed to highlight the stories of children and families connected to Hyundai Hope on Wheels. The campaign extends into hospitals through a partnership with Brave Gowns, transforming traditional hospital gowns into “Warrior Gowns” featuring armour-inspired designs intended to help children feel empowered during treatment. More than 6,000 gowns are expected to be distributed to hospitals through 2026, giving the campaign’s warrior theme a physical presence beyond the advertising. This  professional campaign titled 'The Mark of a Warrior - Little Warriors' was published in United States in September, 2026. It was created for the brands: Hyundai and Hyundai Hope on Wheels, by ad agency: Innocean. The new spot, “Hit the Road” debuts Monday, Sept. 14, as ESPN kicks off its 2026-27 season coverage during Monday Night Football between the Denver Broncos and Kansas City Chiefs. “Hit the Road” is headlined by Joe Buck & Troy Aikman, who will call their 7th Super Bowl overall, and features more than 20 total ESPN talent. description: With autumn the year’s most notoriously unpredictable month, F&F’s AW ‘26 campaign leans into the season by channelling one of haute couture’s hottest trends: tarot. ‘Whatever You’re Dealt’ is a new multi-channel campaign from BBH London that borrows the cultural currency of tarot to capture the idea that, whatever the day or the season throws at you, F&F has the clothes for it. At the heart of the campaign is an F&F tarot deck to help customers predict and prepare for whatever they’re dealt this autumn. Custom made by artist Mr Cut + Stick featuring the new AW ‘26 collection across fashion, menswear and home, the imagery was all shot by fashion and portrait photographer Willow Williams. The deck is made up of 22 Major Arcana cards, as well as a further 56 Minor Arcana cards that take creative cues from the elements, autumnal vistas and other artistic motifs that run throughout the OOH, AV and Social. The social campaign sees fashion creators launch the collection with content inspired by the F&F cards, a series of mini tarot readings and a two-part intro to Tarot series, with tarot reader and creator @tarotwithhollyx. Social audiences will also be able to shop each look online with shoppable cards. The mystical TV slot also takes its cues from tarot and was shot by award-winning film director Olivia De Camps, renowned for her work with The Ordinary and billie. The ad shows a woman coping with various unpredictable surprises as she navigates a city’s streets in the autumn, with every scenario saved by F&F outfits. Rachel Nooney, Head of Brand and Marketing at F&F said: “We can’t predict the future, especially with all the changes autumn throws our way. But while any brand can talk about layering, we wanted to arm our customers to Style it Out whatever the season throws at them. Through the world of tarot, we found a unique lens that has a rich history in high fashion, has hugely permeated pop culture and centres around the ability to predict or prepare for whatever you’re dealt this autumn.” The campaign comes as part of F&F’s broader brand platform from BBH, ‘Style it out’, that reminds shoppers that F&F has an outfit for every day and every situation life may bring. ‘Whatever You’re Dealt’ will roll out across TV, social media, digital, press and OOH. This includes London's Piccadilly Lights, with visuals leaning heavily into the aesthetics of the centuries-old world of tarot. F&F is also taking over Frameless art gallery in London’s Marylebone on 17th September during London Fashion Week to launch the collection via an immersive tarot experience for press and influencers. description: HARIBO, the UK’s number one confectionery brand, is launching a major new out-of-home campaign for Starmix, bringing its enduring celebration of childlike happiness to life in a new way. Created by long-standing strategic and creative partners Quiet Storm, the campaign takes HARIBO’s much-loved creative platform into an image-led medium, using its iconic Starmix shapes as the starting point for playful imagination. The idea draws on something at the heart of the brand: HARIBO brings out the inner child in all of us. Inspired by the instinctive childhood act of seeing characters and stories in everyday objects, Starmix’s instantly recognisable shapes become the creative material. The campaign brings to life a butterfly bursting into flight, a blazing rocket and a roaring dinosaur stomping the ground, each created from Starmix and signed off by the adults who imagined them. The work also extends into 3D out-of-home, taking the creations beyond the poster and bringing them to life in the real world. The campaign forms part of HARIBO’s wider brand platform, finding new ways to express its enduring celebration of childlike happiness across different channels. It comes as brands adapt to a changing media landscape following the introduction of HFSS advertising restrictions, demonstrating how an established creative platform can continue to evolve within the channels available to it. Massimo Fiori, Managing Director at Quiet Storm, said: “Starmix has always been a brilliant invitation to play. Its familiar shapes give you somewhere to start, then your imagination does the rest. This campaign captures that simple moment when a sweet becomes something entirely unexpected.” The campaign runs across the UK and Republic of Ireland. Philip Murphy, Chief Marketing Officer, HARIBO UK and Ireland: “Starmix was first created over 30 years ago. Since then, it has sparked playful imagination for millions of fans across the UK to become one of the nation’s favourite sweets. Our new creative shows limitless possibilities when you let your imagination run free with the iconic pieces of Starmix. We hope it reminds everyone of that feeling of childlike joy – no matter your age!” This  professional campaign titled 'Starmix' was published in United Kingdom in September, 2026. It was created for the brand: HARIBO, by ad agency: Quiet Storm. This Integrated and OOH Outdoor media campaign is related to the Candy, Snacks industry and contains 6 media assets. description: To celebrate the arrival of its new Peakfreak™ hiking shoe, Columbia Sportswear is launching the F££T FUND, offering hikers cold hard cash for photos of their feet. The social campaign taps into the booming feet pics business, predicted to be worth £1.9 billion by the end of the year (Statista), by giving away cash for photos of bare feet taken in the wilderness. But unlike the rest of the internet, Columbia isn’t interested in tootsies in the wikiFeet sense, it’s focused on what great footwear can do for them. The campaign kicks off with a series of teasers across social platforms including TikTok, Instagram and Snapchat. Then, outdoor influencers will share screenshots of what appears to be a private direct message from Columbia asking them for feet pics. The messages are real. To reveal what's actually going on, creator James Norbury has published an unboxing video with a difference. Rather than using their hands, they are unboxing a pair of the new Peakfreak™ hiking shoes using only their feet. Shoes are lifted from the box with toes. Tissue paper is peeled back with feet. The creator campaign, which is running across markets in EMEA, culminates with Columbia announcing that it’s officially paying for feet pics. To enter the F££T FUND, followers simply need to DM Columbia a photo of their bare feet taken outdoors on a hike. Selected entries will receive a £135 payment directly from Columbia, enough to purchase a pair of Peakfreak™ shoes to protect their most prized assets. Winning entries will be featured in the Hall of Feet, a social gallery celebrating the finest examples of trail-tested toes. “We designed the new Peakfreak™ to keep hikers comfortable across long journeys, challenging terrains and unpredictable conditions. But instead of talking about our innovations in cushioning, traction and support, we’re shining a spotlight on the thing the shoe is built to protect - your feet.” Issam Djemel, Europe Footwear Director. Ant Nelson, Chief Creative Officer at adam&eve\TBWA, said: “Hikers proudly share snaps of mountain summits and epic views, but the feet that carried them there rarely get any recognition. The F££T FUND is here to change that. Stepping away from the standard glossy, earnest outdoor ads, Columbia is making a pedicured pivot, once again proving that its gear really is Engineered For Whatever.” This  professional campaign titled 'F££T FUND' was published in United States in September, 2026. It was created for the brand: Columbia Sportswear, by ad agency: adam&eve\TBWA. This Integrated medium campaign is related to the Sportswear industry and contains 8 media assets. It was submitted 1 day ago.

video_title: The Cornish Company — The Great Cornish Heist
description: The Cornish Company has cast a baker, a fudge maker, and an afternoon tea artisan as small-time smugglers for its first ever national TV advert, The Great Cornish Heist, created and produced by Birmingham creative agency Tribera. “The Delicious Rebellion” advert is airing on ITV from September, and brings to life The Cornish Company’s new brand platform underlined with a nod of the region's heritage. From platform to film The Cornish Company was founded in November 2020, sat at their dad’s kitchen table brothers Tom and James Woodley had an idea to share the best of Cornwall, bringing joy and celebration by creating hampers of authentic Cornish food and drink. By 2026, the business had blossomed and the brand started the hunt for a creative partner who could turn the new brand platform “A Delicious Rebellion” to life in 30". They wanted bold, witty and full of character, just like its wonderful people. In addition, it needed to feel authentically Cornish, while also standing apart from more traditional hamper brands. “The Cornish Company came to us with a brand platform they had developed, that had an edge that set them apart,” said Dan Osadciw, Creative Director at Tribera. “It was our job to tell a story about the best of Cornwall, from the perspective of those in the know. We wanted to create something that felt personal, established an emotional connection with the audience, and drove purchase intent – all wrapped up in a contemporary and cheeky Cornish tone.” The idea: The Great Cornish Heist The TV film follows three producers smuggling their wares to the rest of the nation - a baker, a fudge maker, and a cream tea artisan - as they sneak Cornwall’s best produce into a hamper, each caught in a freeze frame with their own on-brand alias: The Pastie Pincher, The Fudge-y Smuggler, and The West Country Scone’drel. It resolves with the hamper passed hand to hand, all the way to a customer’s front door. “We wanted to create three characters who are in on the act,” said Dan. “The Pastie Pincher, The Fudge-y Smuggler, The West Country Scone’drel - it has an Ocean’s Eleven tone with a wink, not menace - right through to the hamper landing on someone’s doorstep.” One shoot day, a full suite of assets The same production day generated the 30-second hero film, three 10-second cutdowns in 9:16, 1:1 and 16:9 for social, freeze-frame paid social statics, hamper product stills for paid ads, the pause screen, and behind-the-scenes content. “One production day had to work incredibly hard,” said Dan. “We built everything around the hero film from the outset, so a single shoot gave The Cornish Company a whole host of content – TV, VOD, paid social, stills, the lot.” Sophie Handley, Head of Marketing at The Cornish Company, added: “We spoke to a few different creative agencies, but Tribera’s creativity stood out from the offset. Everything has been incredibly organised, and we’ve had some honest conversations along the way, which helped us land on the direction, and deliver a TV brand campaign we’re really proud of.” Tribera led creative on the campaign, working alongside The Production Booth on production. This  professional campaign titled 'The Great Cornish Heist' was published in United Kingdom in September, 2026. It was created for the brand: The Cornish Company, by ad agency: Tribera. video_title: Menabrea — The best isn't always best known.
description: Menabrea, the premium Italian Alpine lager, has today launched its first branded short film, ’The best isn't always best known,’ created with independent creative agency ARK Agency, produced by production house, ARTCLASS. For the last 180 years Menabrea has been one of Italy's most quietly respected beers, a story it was keen to share with UK drinkers. The new campaign sets out to highlight Menabrea’s position as ‘Italy’s best kept secret’ giving people a reason to lean in and discover the brand for themselves. At its centre is a long-form piece of branded content - a cinematic short film that imagines a possible story behind the beer's mysterious, under-the-radar reputation. The film will run in Everyman cinemas across the country, marking Menabrea's first foray into short film. Set against the backdrop of Italian history, this "...storia completamente inventata," follows the adventures of a smuggler, La Contrabbandiera, as she roars through the Italian countryside, her contraband, Menabrea beer, safely stowed in her sidecar. Helped by an amusing gaggle of nuns, she evades the law, until a snitch exposes her identity. Captured and incarcerated, with no hope of escape, her sisters hatch a cunning plan to rescue their fearless protagonist, ensuring Menabrea is, once again, merrily on its way. The work was developed through an unusually open, collaborative process: rather than briefing a single fixed idea, ARK invited director Nalle Sjöblad and production company ARTCLASS to respond to the brand's "best kept secret" positioning with their own creative interpretation. Working with producer Craig Dixon and director of photography Max Smeds, captured on 16mm film – the outcome sees a film shaped as much by directorial vision as agency strategy. Eleanor Quigley, Senior Brand Manager, Menabrea, said: “Not every Italian icon needs to shout about itself. For more than 180 years, Menabrea's story has been rooted in Biella, a small Alpine town in northern Italy that's a world away from the Italy most people think they know. We wanted this campaign to have a knowing wink to it, celebrating the joy of discovering something brilliant before everyone else does. ARK and ARTCLASS brought that idea to life beautifully, creating a film that feels less like a beer advert and more like an invitation to uncover one of Italy's best-kept secrets.” Xander Hart, Creative Partner, ARK, said: Beer advertising has become one long ad. The golden-hour terrace, the interchangeable friends, the perfect pour glistening in the sun, and probably David Beckham somewhere in shot. Menabrea saw that too, so when we set out to make this film for their Everyman sponsorship, we agreed early: it had to behave differently. What followed was a genuinely collaborative process with Nalle Sjöblad and the team at ArtClass. We're proud of what we've made together. A film that pulls Menabrea out of the category clichés and back toward the golden age of beer advertising. Nalle Sjöblad, Director, ARTCLASS, said: "Most briefs arrive half-finished; they hand you an answer and ask you to decorate it. This one handed us a feeling, a framework and a line, the best isn't always the best known and trusted us to go and find the film inside it. That trust is rare, and it's the whole reason work like this can rise above advertising into something bigger." The film will go live the evening of the 14th September across Everyman cinemas and paid social, with further activity to follow. This  professional campaign titled 'The best isn't always best known.' was published in United Kingdom in September, 2026. It was created for the brand: Menabrea, by ad agencies: ARK Agency and ArtClass. This Film medium campaign is related to the Alcoholic Drinks industry and contains 1 media asset. video_title: PROSPER GLOBAL — Never Settle for Survival
description: At a time when global funding for aid is under increasing pressure, one of the world’s leading humanitarian organizations, Mercy Corps, launched a new brand identity and campaign that raises expectations about what aid can achieve. The organization has become PROSPER GLOBAL and is kicking off a multi-channel awareness campaign led by M+C Saatchi North America to introduce the new brand and challenge Americans to think differently about humanitarian aid. "NEVER SETTLE FOR SURVIVAL" is a creative campaign that captures an audaciously optimistic belief: barely enough is not enough for anyone, and that meeting urgent survival needs should be the floor, not the ceiling, of ambition for humanitarian aid. The campaign launched with a :30 hero spot that captures the spirit and ingenuity of people around the world who believe we can do more when we refuse to settle for barely enough. It features the dynamic, resilient faces and environments of people who are building what’s next for their communities despite challenges like conflict, climate change fallout and economic hardship. See launch spot here. The campaign is supported by an integrated approach including digital ads, social content, out-of-home, and creators whose work spans sustainability, innovation, health, culture, and community-building activating across social channels. Rather than speak on behalf of communities, the campaign puts stories and perspectives at the center. Work was performed across the M+C Saatchi North America network, including SS+K, Consulting, and Performance. "Humanitarian organizations understandably spend a lot of time communicating urgency and need. With ‘Never Settle for Survival,’ we wanted to start somewhere different: with people’s ambition,” said Giselle Benatar, Vice President of Marketing, Prosper Global. “‘Never Settle for Survival’ looks beyond the crisis and focuses on what people and communities are already building, rather than defining them by the crises they face. It invites people who share our belief that barely enough is not enough for anyone to join us in building a future where people everywhere can prosper and no one is left behind.” "Prosper Global is a rare organization that dares to take on the status quo at a time when the world's biggest problems are only growing,”  said Kevin Skobac, Managing Director, Strategy, SS+K. “‘Never Settle for Survival' captures the spirit and ambition of people around the world taking charge of their own stories.” The “Never Settle” campaign also launches alongside new research from Prosper Global’s Voices of Prosperity Initiative, which asked over 1,100 community members in six countries where Prosper Global works what it means to prosper. In five of six countries surveyed, fewer than 10 percent of people associated prosperity with material wealth. Instead, they talked about safety, community, and the ability to imagine and plan for a future—educating their children, growing a business, making choices about what comes next. This  professional campaign titled 'Never Settle for Survival' was published in United States in September, 2026. It was created for the brand: PROSPER GLOBAL, by ad agency: M+C Saatchi North America. This Film and Integrated media campaign is related to the Public Interest industry and contains 2 media assets. video_title: Cesar — We Should Totally Just Eat CESAR
description: Every fall, one of the internet's most beloved pop culture traditions takes over social media as fans celebrate October 3 with iconic quotes, pink fashion and nostalgic throwbacks. This year, the CESAR® brand is joining forces with actress, mom and dog lover Lacey Chabert to give dogs their own starring role in the fun. Known for her iconic role as an unapologetic, pink-clad trendsetter famous for spilling secrets, Lacey and the CESAR brand are putting a fresh, furry spin on one of cinema's most legendary rants, declaring: We should totally "Just Eat CESAR!" The playful, social-first campaign celebrates dogs, mealtime and the everyday bond they share with the people who love them, headlined by the launch of the limited-edition CESAR Pink Pack, created for pet parents who embody the spirit of Love Like Crazy™. "While Wednesdays will always belong to the color pink, CESAR cuisine provides wholesome, nutritious meals dogs deserve every day," said Lacey Chabert. "We shouldn't save the good stuff for a rare treat! As a dog lover, I'm thrilled to help the CESAR brand show pet parents that giving their dogs high-quality food is the best daily routine." The CESAR brand and Lacey Chabert bring the campaign to life this fall with exclusive drops of the CESAR Pink Pack on Wednesday, September 16 and Wednesday, September 23 at CESAR.com/JustEatCesar, because on Wednesdays (and every day), dogs should Just Eat CESAR!* The limited-edition CESAR Pink Pack invites pet parents and their dogs to become cafeteria royalty with a 12-pack bundle featuring tongue-out tasty CESAR wet food recipes, including: Classic Loaf in Sauce Porterhouse Steak Flavor Filets in Gravy Prime Rib Flavor Classic Loaf in Sauce Smoked Bacon & Egg Flavor Crafted with high-quality, purposeful ingredients, each recipe delivers a 100% complete and balanced nutrition, making the CESAR brand a wholesome, delicious meal dogs deserve every day. "We're thrilled to unveil the re-energized visual identity for our brand – a fresh glow-up of our logo, beloved Westie dog, and new signature color: pink," said Lina Tinsley, Brand Director for CESAR U.S. "With this new campaign, we're bringing that pink identity to life, giving pet parents a fun new way to celebrate a pop culture moment and show their dogs extra love. Because at its heart, CESAR is all about flavorful variety, quality nutrition, and delightful shared experiences." The celebration doesn't stop with the Pink Pack. Lacey Chabert will bring the drama (the good kind!) to social media through a series of exclusive social videos, giving fans a front-row seat to see what makes the CESAR brand the queen bee of pet food with its slow-cooked and perfectly balanced recipes. Fans are encouraged to claim the exclusive drop and share their own, pink-inspired moments with their dog — whether it's a CESAR Pink Pack, a pink pup accessory, or their dog's best "posse" post. Fans can tag @cesardogfood_us on Instagram and @cesardogfood on TikTok using #CESARShare to officially join the "Just Eat CESAR!" squad. Every CESAR Pink Pack also includes an insert card linking directly to Go Fetch Rewards on the Fetch App, where pet parents can earn points and unlock rewards for their pups.* This  professional campaign titled 'We Should Totally Just Eat CESAR' was published in United States in September, 2026. It was created for the brands: Cesar and Mars Petcare, . This Film and Integrated media campaign is related to the Pets industry and contains 3 media assets. It was submitted about 23 hours ago.

video_title: People Like Us — Reject the Rejections
description: New research from non-profit People Like Us and Censuswide reveals that automated hiring software now stands between UK jobseekers and work, rejecting candidates within minutes, sometimes before applications have even closed. The impact falls hardest on ethnic minority jobseekers. People Like Us is calling for greater checks and balances on the automation and AI tools reshaping recruitment. Used well, they serve a real purpose in managing huge volumes of applicants, but their use must be disclosed before candidates apply, accountable to a human when challenged, and independently audited for bias. The survey of 2,000 UK job seekers found that 80% have been rejected in the past two years and of those, nearly three quarters (74%) suspect at least one rejection was generated automatically without a human reading their application. And they may never find out as just 15% of candidates say an employer has told them an automated system was used. Ethnically diverse candidates are hit disproportionately as they apply for a third more roles than white counterparts, are rejected faster (41% within an hour of applying vs 32%), and are significantly more likely to remove elements of their identity from their CVs to get past automated systems (70% compared to 57%). Erasing parts of identity pre-dates automations and AI with decades of UK research on name bias demonstrating how this has been impacting workers, however automations add speed and scale and remove the person who could be asked why. In response to the findings, People Like Us have launched Reject the Rejections, a new campaign created in partnership with creative agency Worth Your While. The campaign has several objectives: to raise awareness among rejected job applicants that they may have the right to request a human review of their application if they suspect the decision was made by automation; to urge employers to disclose the use of automation in their hiring processes and commit to independent bias audits; and finally, to call on the government to consider screening transparency laws. At the heart of the campaign is a powerful 4 minute short film starring British actor Ebenezer Gyau (Amandaland, Black Mirror, Suspect). Directed by critically acclaimed director Amara Abbas through new—land productions, Dear [Name] transforms the language of real rejection emails sent to real ethnic minority candidates into a powerful spoken-word performance about hope, exclusion and the invisible barriers facing talented candidates. Set inside an anonymous waiting room separated by a two-way mirror, the film follows a talented candidate rehearsing the familiar language of corporate rejection emails. As each carefully worded "thank you for your application" unfolds, the audience hears the internal dialogue those messages leave behind - self-doubt, resilience, frustration and ultimately a challenge back to the system itself. In addition to the film, People Like Us has is arming candidates with a tool to Reject the Rejections, developed with Planes Studio that any rejected candidate can send in just two clicks to ask whether an automation was used on their application and remind job seekers they may have the right to request a human review under existing UK Data Protection laws. The tool is here: https://rejections.plu.org.uk/individuals#request-a-human-review The findings build on a recent substantial analysis of over 100,000 live graduate applications from UCL which reveal ethnic minority candidates are well represented in application pools for graduate roles but are disproportionately rejected at the initial screening and online testing stage of recruitment despite having similar qualifications. This suggests employer outreach efforts to diversify applicant pools have been successful while adverse impact during recruitment processes remains. JCDecaux Community Channel is supporting the campaign over autumn, with an initial run across 19 large-format digital sites in London this Wednesday, generating an estimated 154,000 impressions, ahead of a fuller national campaign launching in November. A 30-second cut of the film will also run as a two-week national cinema campaign in partnership with Pearl & Dean from 2 October, screening alongside major releases including Sense & Sensibility, Heart of the Beast, Digger and Verity. This  professional campaign titled 'Reject the Rejections' was published on September 16, 2026. It was created for the brand: People Like Us, by ad agency: Worth Your While. description: Having spent years working together at Atomic London, COO & Creative Director Andrew Nethercleft, Producer Alex Coxhill, and Andrew ‘Pooley’ Poole (Director, Senior Editor and Motion Animator) have reteamed under Coxhill & Co to develop and produce Remember A Charity's latest campaign. Building on a long-standing, trusted relationship with the client, we delivered the project as a lean core team, keeping the emphasis entirely on sharp creative, direct collaboration, and efficient production. Remember A Charity is a collective of around 200 UK charities working to champion legacy giving across the nation by inspiring more people to leave a gift in their Will to causes they care about. The 'Be Remembered' campaign celebrates real human eccentricities through warmth and character-driven humour. By leaning into the memorable quirks that define who we are, the spots highlight how meaningful and accessible legacy giving can be, framing it as a lasting celebration of a person’s unique story. Voiced by actor Pearce Quigley (Small Prophets, Detectorists, The Gentlemen), the spots bring these personal quirks to life, reframing how legacy gifts are introduced to UK audiences. Andrew Poole, Director: "The 'Be Remembered' concept hinges on the small, idiosyncratic quirks that make people unmistakably themselves, so my focus was on capturing authentic human warmth over traditional charity tropes. Pearce Quigley’s voiceover anchored that dry, character-driven British humour perfectly. From battling the chaotic weather and putting all my trust in an app to tell me when the sun would break through the rain, so I could bag the shots I needed to depict a summer tandem bike ride, to the intimate interior setups for Gamer. We focused on the subtle characteristic mannerisms and humorous performances of our actors, such as Gloria kicking out the kitchen chair for her grandson like a card shark, or Derek missing his mouth with the water bottle, to make these characters instantly recognisable." Lucinda Frostick, Director at Remember a Charity: “We couldn’t be happier with the new Be Remembered films. The characters are funny, memorable and wonderfully human, and they capture something we all recognise – that we’re often remembered for the little things that make us who we are. We hope the films make people smile, while also getting them thinking about the causes they’d like to support in the future.” This  professional campaign titled 'Be Remembered' was published in United Kingdom in September, 2026. It was created for the brand: Remember A Charity, . This Film medium campaign is related to the Other industry and contains 6 media assets. It was submitted about 4 hours ago.

description: OneDome is taking its successful “The New Way” campaign nationwide from today, following a strong response to its eight-week regional television campaign across the South of England. The regional campaign ran across May, June, and July and reached three million television viewers. The 30-second film has also received more than two million views on YouTube. The national rollout begins today and will run for six weeks until the end of October. It is expected to reach a further 7.6 million viewers across Britain. The first national 30-second advert will air during Channel 4 News at 7.35pm tonight. Further spots will appear during Channel 4 News and Amazing Spaces: First Homes throughout September. The campaign will continue during October with a mix of 10-second and 30-second adverts. “The New Way” contrasts two very different homebuying experiences. The “Old Way” leaves buyers coordinating separate mortgage brokers, conveyancers, surveyors, and insurers. The campaign uses humour to capture the chasing, confusion, and pressure this can create. The “New Way” introduces OneDome’s alternative. It brings the essential services together through one coordinated homebuying service, supported by one team and one place to follow the purchase. The national rollout marks the next major phase of OneDome’s largest brand campaign to date. It builds on the success of the regional campaign, and brings the company’s message to millions more homebuyers across Britain. Paul Troy, chief marketing officer at OneDome, said: “The campaign uses humour to show a situation that homebuyers know all too well. Different people hold different pieces of the purchase, while the buyer is left chasing everyone and trying to make sense of it all. “Our eight-week regional campaign reached three million television viewers, while the full-length film has now passed two million views on YouTube. The national rollout is the next major step and is expected to reach a further 7.6 million viewers across Britain. “We want people to question why buying a home still feels so complicated, and to know that they no longer have to accept the Old Way.” The campaign was developed with global marketing network Stagwell, alongside Forsman & Bodenfors, and Goodstuff. It is backed by a £7.5 million media-for-equity partnership with Channel 4 Ventures. Babek Ismayil, founder and CEO of OneDome, said: “Homebuyers should not have to become project managers just to buy a home. Yet they are still expected to coordinate different companies, chase updates and carry the risk when the process goes wrong. “We built OneDome because the system should work around the buyer, not the other way around. The response to the regional campaign showed how strongly this problem resonates with people. “Taking The New Way national allows us to reach millions more homebuyers and show them that there is now a simpler, more coordinated way to buy a home.” This  professional campaign titled 'The New Way' was published in United Kingdom in September, 2026. It was created for the brand: OneDome, by ad agencies: Forsman & Bodenfors and Stagwell. This Film medium campaign is related to the Real Estate industry and contains 1 media asset. It was submitted 8 minutes ago.

video_title: Jersey Mike’s — Game Day Mike’s Way
description: Jersey Mike’s is introducing a new platform for its second year of partnership with the NFL, called “Game Day Mike’s Way.” Created with Highdive as an extension of last year’s "Eli vs. Danny" platform that introduced Danny DeVito and Eli Manning's on-brand rivalry, this year’s platform launches with a biopic-style short film “Stacked and Jacked: The Danny DeVito Story.” In the film, Danny develops a strong arm from years of hoisting Jersey Mike’s subs loaded with an abundance of meat, cheese and toppings, allowing him to ultimately become the best quarterback the NFL has ever seen while Eli watches from the sidelines. When asked, “How do you keep that golden arm in shape?” Danny responds, “It’s easy. Lift heavy sub, eat heavy sub.” Behind the joke. Since Jersey Mike's subs are loaded with so much meat, cheese and toppings, we wanted to take it to the extreme by showing what happens to our #1 fan, Danny DeVito. “Stacked and Jacked” tells the story of the natural conclusion of lifting so many heavy subs: you develop a jacked arm and become a pro QB in the NFL. In this alternate reality, Danny rockets to football stardom, much to the disbelief of his Jersey Mike's rival and former Giants QB, Eli Manning. A rivalry with a twist. This new platform marks the second time Danny and Eli have starred in a campaign together. Last year, Eli became a new spokesperson for the brand's NFL sponsorship, and Danny took it as Eli trying to take his job. So, after Eli stole Danny's job in Year 1, this year Danny's the one taking the field, and Eli's watching from the sidelines. The most integrated Jersey Mike's campaign to date. This year, we created a whole world for Danny's QB story to live in. The campaign spans TV, OLV, social, display, influencer, brand acts and limited edition products. Comedic creative pedigree. Director Eric Appel is known for creating faux trailers for biopic-style movies, including the viral Weird Al and Field of Dreams 2. This approach is right in his sweet spot: a film that plays out like a classic sports movie, where the underdog becomes a star. This  professional campaign titled 'Game Day Mike’s Way' was published in United States in September, 2026. It was created for the brand: Jersey Mike’s, by ad agency: Highdive. description: Nutrafol is challenging the traditional before-and-after. In a category obsessed with dramatic transformations and instant results, Nutrafol’s newest campaign, “Be An After” shifts the focus from the final outcome to the choice that starts meaningful change. About the Campaign: Created in partnership with nice&frank, “Be An After” reframes the moment of transformation. Rather than waiting until you’ve reached the finish line to call yourself an “after,” Nutrafol believes you become one the moment you recognize something needs to change and choose to invest in yourself. Hair growth is part of that journey, but the emotional outcome is bigger: feeling like yourself again. The Creative: The creative turns the familiar before-and-after format on its head. Each film opens on a stereotypical before-and-after, then rewinds from the visible outcome through the messy, meaningful moments that came before it, ultimately landing on the decision to begin. Told through stories of postpartum, divorce and marathon training, the campaign connects hair growth with broader moments of personal growth. After a Baby…Choosing Yourself: A new mom’s hair before-and-after rewinds through the realities of early motherhood to reveal the moment she chooses to prioritize herself and her hair health, reframing her “after” as the decision to invest in herself, not simply the visible result. After a Marathon…Choosing to Keep Going: A marathoner’s before-and-after rewinds from the finish line through the setbacks and discipline of training to the moment he first notices his thinning hair, connecting the consistency required to pursue a personal goal with the choice to take action to support his hair health journey. After a Divorce…Choosing Your Next Chapter: A woman’s before-and-after rewinds through life after divorce to the moment she recognizes stress-related thinning and chooses to invest in herself, celebrating an “after” defined not just by healthier hair, but by moving forward and feeling like herself again. The Media Plan: “Be An After” will come to life on paid media channels across online, social, broadcast, launching with linear spots debuting on TV’s biggest night (Sept. 14). Nutrafol will tap into the moment and shift the spotlight to what came before those moments: the choices, consistency and work that got people to the red carpet in the first place. Real Growth comes to life in major cultural moments where growth and achievement are on display. The awards show gives Nutrafol a powerful stage to celebrate not just the polished “after” on the red carpet, but the ambition, preparation and years of work behind the people who bring our most beloved television to life. In partnership with red carpet correspondent Zanna Roberts Rassi and Live From E!, Nutrafol will go behind the scenes of preparation while celebrating the years of experience behind Zanna’s own journey as a Nutrafol user, bringing Real Growth to life through a personal story of evolution and achievement. Showing up around one of entertainment’s biggest nights reflects the growing reach of Nutrafol and Real Growth -- bringing the brand into premium cultural moments, reaching broader audiences and expanding the conversation around growth beyond hair alone. description: Iris Kim, a prolific commercial, music video and film director who is represented by CANADA in the U.S., has directed an acutely observed slice of immigrant life for Kotn, the progressive New York based apparel brand. The one minute long social media film captures Nataly as she hastily gathers herself and her luggage for a flight to visit family overseas, running into friends and familiar faces in her immigrant community who help along the way. “We wanted this whole project to feel playful and relatable to immigrant kids who grow up feeling like they live two different lives: one with their family and one with everyone else,” said Kim. “I loved the idea of taking these really ordinary moments and heightening them into something a little more dramatic. There was so much personality in the cast and the clothes, so a big part of directing involved creating space for those interactions and letting the humour come through in a fun and punchy way. Everyone really leaned into the world we were creating, which made the whole thing so much fun to shoot.” Kotn is a certified B Corporation voted Best for the World™, with the fourth-highest B Impact Score of apparel brands in North America. With each order, the company invests in the creation of jobs, infrastructure, systems, and education to alleviate poverty and create shared, sustainable growth for the communities they are part of. Kim has worked on a wide range of global brands including MAC, L’Oreal, Vinted, Liquid IV, WNBA, Nike, Google, Waymo, among others. Her music video direction includes work for Interscope Records, Universal Music, Giant Music and Republic Records. Inspired by 90’s rom-coms, with an added dose of raw edginess, Kim’s work is characterized by an abundance of color, humor and fashion. video_title: Hargreaves Lansdown — Don’t Tolerate Inactive Banks
description: Hargreaves Lansdown, the UK’s largest investments platform, has today launched a new TV spot for its Active Savings product, as part of its biggest savings campaign to date. The work is Stitchy’s first above-the-line campaign since its appointment by Hargreaves Lansdown. The film is the latest phase of the multi-million pound integrated ‘Don’t Tolerate Inactive Banks’ campaign, with activity across OOH, print, social and creator channels already live, and VOD launching alongside TV. The push aims to make Active Savings famous as a better way to save, challenging the hold established banks have over people’s money and positioning Hargreaves Lansdown as a credible home for savings as well as investments. The campaign is based on the insight that many people with significant cash savings – typically £10,000 to £20,000 or more – leave their money with a familiar bank through habit, trust or loyalty, even when they could be getting more from it elsewhere. Stitchy’s creative idea uses the Active Savings product name to define its opposite: inactive banks. By giving banking complacency a name, ‘Don’t Tolerate Inactive Banks’ reframes established banks as institutions that benefit when customers leave their savings unquestioned, while positioning Hargreaves Lansdown Active Savings as the alternative. Directed by Ben Green at Bullion, the drily humorous 30-second film takes viewers inside an ‘inactive bank’, populated by yawning staff, unanswered phones and employees finding increasingly inventive ways to pass the time. Creator Rob Madin, best known for his comedy alter-ego Brett Domino, stars as a banker presenting a poor savings rate as though it were a generous reward for years of loyalty. His misplaced confidence, set against the lethargy of the bank around him, exposes the gap between the reassuring language of banking and what customers may actually be getting in return. Stitchy also brought in BAFTA-nominated writer, director, actor and comedian David Schneider as comedy craft consultant, helping sharpen the ad’s characterisation, timing and physical comedy. The humour comes at the expense of the banks rather than their customers, creating a comic world in which the entertainment carries the argument: the more inactive the bank appears, the more viewers are invited to question what their loyalty is earning them. The film reflects Stitchy’s post-social approach to creativity, taking what social has taught brands about earning attention through recognisable behaviour, distinctive characters and moments people actually want to watch, and applying that thinking to TV. Rather than treating TV and social as separate creative worlds, the campaign is designed to travel between channels. Madin’s creator sensibility is brought into the TV performance, while shorter social films extend the bankers’ time-wasting behaviour into individual comic scenarios. OOH and print distil the idea into pointed challenges to banking loyalty and complacency, while creator activity brings the issue closer to people’s own savings habits. video_title: The School Food Project — Serving up the school food crisis on a plate
description: To coincide with the government's rollout of updated school food standards, BBH London has worked with The School Food Project on a campaign to show parents the real quality of school food, and how they can help change it. The School Food Project has been created by a coalition of charities and food organisations dedicated to improving child nutrition and school food across the UK including Bite Back, Chefs in Schools, School Food Matters, The Food Foundation and the Jamie Oliver Group. The coalition has been set up to support schools to transform school food, improve food education and serve delicious meals to children and young people up and down the country. For the launch, BBH London created a fake pop-up tasting experience fronted by renowned British chef Angela Hartnett, to serve real school meals to unsuspecting diners. The activation was based on a simple insight: while the debate around school food is often framed around children's experiences, adults may respond differently if they were confronted with the same food themselves. The aim is to start a nationwide movement that empowers families to demand healthier, higher-quality school meals while encouraging schools and catering providers to raise food standards. Named Centena, an anagram of 'canteen', the experience was presented to guests as Angela Hartnett's latest dining venture. In reality, she designed neither the dishes nor the menu. Instead, diners were first surprised by being served school meals, including processed chicken burgers, stale burger buns, soggy chips and cold, congealed baked beans before being shown what good looks like through dishes designed to demonstrate that a change in school food standards is possible. Guests' reactions were captured for a social media film directing people to the project's website hub created to empower families to sign their schools up for help from the School Food Project. Naomi Duncan, CEO of Chefs in Schools, one of the School Food Project partners said, "This is a huge moment for school food. What we consistently hear from children and young people is that they care about taste, flavour and nutrition and are far more willing to be adventurous with food than we might imagine. New standards mean an exciting opportunity to translate Government ambition into tasty food that children will enjoy. The School Food Project has been set up to support schools and caterers to make that transition, and we hope many schools will sign up to our Hub for support as the new standards are released." Karen Martin, CEO of BBH London and Dublin said: "The work the School Food Project is doing is vital: to show parents that good school food really is possible. We're so proud to have supported members of the Project's coalition for many years now and look forward to working together moving forwards." The campaign launch coincides with the government rollout of updated school food standards, with a particular focus on secondary schools. Changes in school food standards are due to be enforced from September 2027, but the government is expecting schools to roll out healthier meal options straight away.
