video_title: Humane World for Animals — Travis Barker Urges Compassionate Choices For Animals in Campaign
description: Travis Barker Urges Compassionate Choices For Animals in New Humane World for Animals Campaign From punk rock bad boy to animal advocate, Barker proves doing good can still have an edge in a new PSA campaign created in tandem with agency partner FlyteVu. Today, Blink-182 drummer and longtime animal lover Travis Barker sheds his bad boy image for a good cause. Barker is teaming up with Humane World for Animals, formerly called the Humane Society of the United States and Humane Society International, to encourage people to take action for animals by implementing Small Steps for Good in their everyday lives. In a new public service announcement created by the Humane World for Animals’s ad agency partner, FlyteVu, the punk rock icon reveals how creating a better future for animals does not require dramatic life changes. Simple choices like eating more plant-based meals, choosing cruelty-free products, embracing animal-friendly fashion or adopting a shelter pet instead of buying one from a pet store can have a big impact on reducing animal suffering. “Doing good is cool, and it doesn’t have to be hard. I've been vegan for years because I care deeply about animals,” said Barker. “Every day, we make choices that reflect what matters to us. Whether it's what we eat, wear or buy, small actions can add up to meaningful change. I'm proud to partner with Humane World for Animals to encourage more people to make choices that help build a better future for animals.” Known for his influential career in music, Barker has been a dedicated advocate for animals for many years. Through his collaboration with Humane World for Animals, Barker is helping raise awareness of issues affecting animals. A vegan since 2008, he has backed that commitment through investments in vegan restaurants, a cruelty-free wellness brand and support for ethical fashion. “Creating a better world for animals takes bold systemic change, and it starts with the small choices people make every day,” said Kitty Block, president and CEO of Humane World for Animals. “That’s the idea behind our Small Steps for Good campaign: Showing that everyone has the power to make a difference for animals. Travis has inspired people for years by using his voice and platform to advocate for animals in a way that is authentic to who he is. We hope this campaign encourages others to discover their own small steps and see how those actions can add up to meaningful change.” To reach Gen Z and millennials, audiences who are deeply passionate about this cause, its agency, FlyteVu, knew it needed to come up with a way to put animal cruelty on consumers’ radars in a way that was culturally relevant, engaging and accessible, while showing how the barrier to doing good doesn’t have to be as hard as one may think. “Who better than one of rock’s most famous bad boys to prove you don’t have to be a saint to do some good? That’s what we loved about Travis,” said FlyteVu Chief Creative Officer Linda Knight. “Travis makes the message unexpected and entertaining, while showing that caring about animals doesn’t require being perfect, playing nice, or changing who you are. You just have to do something. And that something doesn’t have to be huge. Small acts add up.” The campaign spans organic and paid social media ads, as well as CTV ad buys on Paramount+, Tubi and Roku. Future media buys may span Hulu and HBO Max, as well as additional PSA announcements running on national and local television. To learn more about the campaign and find ways to take action for animals, visit humaneworld.org/stepsforgood. description: Sapporo is continuing its “So Pour a Sapporo” platform with “Prepare for Fugu,” a new campaign from Australian indie agency Sunday Gravy offering consumers in Australia and New Zealand the chance to experience one of Japan’s most legendary culinary traditions. Consumers who purchase Sapporo can enter to win a fugu dining experience in Japan, where the potentially poisonous delicacy can only be prepared by highly trained, licensed chefs. To launch the campaign, Sapporo has created a cinematic short film inspired by Japanese psychological thrillers. The film blurs reality and imagination as the fear of being poisoned begins to take over, building an escalating sense of tension and unease around the ritual of eating fugu. The campaign continues the “So Pour a Sapporo” idea of slowing down and appreciating experiences shared over a beer. Sunday Gravy said the life-or-death precision involved in preparing fugu makes the dining ritual an experience that demands complete attention, while the campaign gives audiences the opportunity to experience that tradition for themselves. “Prepare for Fugu” launches nationally across film, cinema, OOH, PR, on-pack, on-premise, digital, social and retail. By combining a dramatic film with a real-world prize, the campaign turns Sapporo’s Japanese heritage into an experience that extends well beyond the beer itself. description: AMV BBDO is introducing a new twist on Currys’ long-running “Beyond Techspectations” platform, this time harnessing the viral/social ‘dad energy’ trend to showcase how their colleagues can help customers apply an energy-saving mindset to their tech at home. In signature Currys style, this latest campaign shares a clear message in a memorable, humorous way by turning the nation’s familiar dad behaviours into comedy and using Currys expertise to help people understand smarter more efficient tech. Currys colleagues remain the stars of the show, becoming larger-than-life “energy-saving dads”, complete with moustaches, dad poses and unsolicited advice on how to be more energy efficient at home. The tongue-in-cheek campaign draws on viral ‘dad energy’ trend and sees Currys colleagues adopting the exaggerated conventions of ‘dad energy’ seen across social media as a way to champion the use of smarter, more efficient tech. The campaign showcases Currys’ colleague as experts in energy efficient technology, demonstrating how its products can help reduce waste across a whole range of life’s essentials that go beyond just your electricity bill. Whether it’s energy, water, food, cleaning products or time, the Currys colleagues in dad mode will find a way to reduce waste with more efficient technology, combining humour with clear product demonstrations. Jez Tribe and Dave Westland, Creative Directors at AMV BBDO, said: “Energy efficiency isn’t an easy topic to bring to life in an entertaining way. So, when we saw the idea of leaning into the dad memes that are all over social media, we knew we could give it a unique spin for Currys.” Martin Burke, Senior Advertising Manager at Currys, said: “Our experts know efficiency is about much more than energy. So, we’re having a bit of fun with ‘dad mode’ to show just how many ways smarter tech can help us reduce waste. By taking the idea to an absurd extreme, Currys is making efficiency memorable, entertaining and culturally relatable, while showcasing the benefits of our products across the home.” The campaign will run until 20th October across VOD, OLV, Radio and Digital Audio in the UK. This  professional campaign titled 'Full Dad Mode' was published in United Kingdom in September, 2026. It was created for the brand: Currys, by ad agency: AMV BBDO. description: What if your next favorite look is already hanging in someone else’s closet? Today, Poshmark introduces Try Yourself On™, a new brand concept debuting as part of the company’s largest integrated brand campaign to-date. Rooted in the belief that personal style is meant to be explored, Try Yourself On celebrates the possibilities found across millions of individual closets and invites fashion lovers to look beyond what they already know they like and discover something unexpected. Launching September 8 during New York’s biggest week in fashion, the campaign brings Try Yourself On to life across film, out-of-home, social and experiential, alongside collaborations with creative voices across fashion and culture. “Poshmark brings millions of expressions of human taste together in one place,” said Elizabeth von der Goltz, Chief Revenue Officer, Poshmark. “You can move between aesthetics, discover a new designer, find an amazing piece from another era, or stumble upon something you never would have searched for. That’s the idea behind ‘Try Yourself On’ - fashion as a way to discover different versions of yourself. There’s no other fashion destination quite like Poshmark where the world’s closets are at your fingertips.” The launch comes amid a broader evolution at Poshmark, as new leadership and industry expertise bring a sharper fashion lens and fresh perspective to the marketplace aimed at building cultural relevance and driving commercial growth. Try Yourself On Developed in partnership with creative agency nice&frank, the Try Yourself On campaign draws inspiration from the curiosity of looking through someone else’s closet and discovering something you might never have searched for yourself. Set against Poshmark’s ever-changing marketplace, where more than 700,000 new listings are added every day, the campaign celebrates the possibilities of personal style and the thrill of trying on something unexpected. A series of long- and short-form films directed by mixed-media director and photographer Léa Esmaili combines live action, animation and CGI to capture the playful spirit of dressing up. The films follow characters through unexpected worlds, outfits and identities as they search for what they had in mind — and discover something they never knew they wanted. Launching September 8, Try Yourself On will extend across New York City, Los Angeles and Toronto through Poshmark’s largest out-of-home campaign to date, including major takeovers of Manhattan’s Union Square and Broadway-Lafayette subway stations and Toronto’s St. George Station. Bringing New Creative Perspectives to Poshmark Throughout Fashion Month, Poshmark is collaborating with a group of distinctive voices across fashion, entertainment, photography and culture to bring their perspectives on personal style and discovery to the campaign. Chloe Fineman, Courtney Grow, Jalil Johnson, Nicky Campbell, Colleen Allen, Elissa Santisi and daughter Francesca Keller, photographer Tyler Joe, Jerry and Zachary Pozniak of Jeeves Dry Cleaners and Poshmark Chief Revenue Officer Elizabeth von der Goltz will participate in a social content series, each interpreting Try Yourself On through their own creative lens. Several will also bring their individual taste directly to Poshmark through new Tastemaker curations, selecting and liking pieces they discover across the marketplace to create curated edits for shoppers. The initiative brings Poshmark closer to the creative community while giving buyers a new source of inspiration and a way to discover product through distinctive points of view on fashion and personal style. Try Yourself On During New York Fashion Week On Sunday, September 13, the campaign will come to life in New York City through the Poshmark Dry Cleaners, an interactive consumer activation in SoHo. Transforming the familiar neighborhood dry cleaner into an unexpected fashion destination, the experience celebrates the idea that some of the most coveted pieces aren’t walking the runway -  they’re already hanging in someone else’s closet. Together, the campaign, creative collaborations and New York Fashion Week activation bring Try Yourself On to life, celebrating the possibilities of personal style and the millions of closets that make Poshmark unlike any other fashion marketplace. This  professional campaign titled 'Try Yourself On' was published in United States in September, 2026. It was created for the brand: Poshmark, by ad agency: nice&frank. description: Today, King's Hawaiian is unveiling "Mmmoments" a new campaign celebrating the launch of Soft Swirl Cinnamon Bites and how this delightful new snack makes everyday moments a little better. Kicking off the campaign, the brand teamed up with Taylor Hanson of the beloved pop-rock trio Hanson to debut "MMMBites," a freshly baked rendition of the iconic 90’s hit "MMMBop" ahead of the legendary song's 30th anniversary. Building on more than 75 years as a family-owned bakery brand, King's Hawaiian has been expanding its snacking portfolio by complementing the 2024 introduction of Soft Pretzel Bites with the launch of new Soft Swirl Cinnamon Bites. Perfectly soft and irresistibly craveable, King's Hawaiian Bites turn everyday moments —even the not-so-fun ones—into something worth smiling about. Whether it's surviving a Monday morning, squeezing into a middle seat on an airplane or simply looking for an afternoon pick-me-up, everything is better with Bites. The campaign comes to life through a series of humorous spots featuring Taylor Hanson making everyday moments better by sharing King's Hawaiian Bites and  launching into the instantly recognizable "MMMBites" chorus. The first spot, Mmmondays, debuted on 9/7. "MMMBop has been stuck in people's heads as a feel-good bop for decades, and while we've had opportunities to reinvent it over the years, none ever felt quite right until now," said Taylor Hanson.  “We thought this was the right opportunity to give it a fresh twist with MMMBites as a fun way to celebrate a snack that's all about bringing a little more joy to everyday life," said Taylor Hanson. "Hopefully people will find themselves singing - and snacking - along." Available now at major grocery retailers nationwide alongside fan-favorite Pretzel Bites, Soft Swirl Cinnamon Bites feature cinnamon swirl baked into every bite, delivering crave-worthy, not-too-sweet cinnamon flavor wrapped inside the signature soft, fluffy King's Hawaiian dough fans know and love. Whether enjoyed straight from the tub or warmed for an extra comforting treat, Soft Swirl Cinnamon Bites are a truly feel-good sweet snack. "King's Hawaiian Bites make any little moment feel better," said Raouf Moussa, Chief Marketing Officer at King's Hawaiian. "As we continue growing our snack portfolio, Soft Swirl Cinnamon Bites are an exciting addition, bringing the King's Hawaiian experience fans know and love to an entirely new sweet occasion - morning snacking." Consumers can learn more about King's Hawaiian Bites at kingshawaiian.com/cinnamon-bites This  professional campaign titled 'Mmmoments' was published in United States in September, 2026. video_title: Legora — Focus where it matters most.
description: Swedish legal tech company Legora turns Aaron Judge’s greatest asset, his ability to shut out the noise and focus on the pitch that matters, into a metaphor for how AI can help legal teams work. Earlier this year, Legora announced a multi-year partnership with Aaron Judge and the New York Yankees. Now, the AI company is activating the partnership in a new campaign — the latest in a string of idea-led work built around an unlikely but deliberate connection to the brand. Previous campaigns have included using Jude Law to turn his own name into the campaign idea, and The Man Behind the Man, which shifted the spotlight from Swedish golf star Ludvig Åberg to his caddie Joe Skovron — a metaphor for the behind-the-scenes support Legora provides legal professionals. This time, that same approach moves to baseball. Built around the line “Focus where it matters most,” the campaign draws a simple connection between Judge’s job at the plate and the work of a lawyer: knowing where your attention makes the biggest difference. That idea is brought to life through a visual device inspired by baseball’s strike zone and MLB’s new ABS Challenge System. As the film progresses, the frame tightens around Judge, shrinking away everything outside the zone until only what demands his full attention remains. The timing is deliberate. Introduced across MLB in 2026, the ABS Challenge System allows disputed ball-and-strike calls to be checked digitally against the strike zone — effectively turning one of baseball’s most familiar judgments into something that can now be visualized and verified in real time. “From the strike zone to legal work, there’s a pretty straight line,” says Stuart Shingler, SVP Brand and Communications at Legora. “For Aaron, it’s about shutting everything else out and focusing entirely on the next pitch. For lawyers, it’s about spending less time on research, administration and other time-consuming work, so they can put more of their attention into the judgment, experience and expertise that make the biggest difference.” Like Legora’s previous sports work, the campaign is shot in black and white — part of an emerging visual and strategic platform for the brand’s sponsorships. “Too many sponsorships stop at a logo and a famous face,” says Erik Nordenankar, Art Director at NoA Åkestam Holst. “We think there has to be an idea behind it — a reason why this person and this brand belong together. For us, a sponsorship should always say something about what Legora stands for, or what it actually does for its customers.” Created by NoA Åkestam Holst, the campaign rolls out across TV, online video and social, alongside OOH and DOOH in New York, including Times Square and a takeover at the 161st Street–Yankee Stadium subway station. This  professional campaign titled 'Focus where it matters most.' was published in Sweden and United States in September, 2026. It was created for the brand: Legora, by ad agency: Åkestam Holst NoA. description: Ross is launching On My Way, an original documentary series following two emerging musicians on separate road trips, with Grammy-nominated artist Khalid joining them at pivotal moments along the way. Created with McKinney and production partner CYLNDR Studios, the series follows Ian Cobiella and Bryce Fleming at turning points in their lives. Ian is considering switching from Computer Science to Music Composition, while Bryce has just graduated and is beginning her career as an artist. Each hits the road with an original song in progress and a destination ahead. Along the way, Khalid steps in at just the right moment, not as a celebrity cameo, but as an artist who understands the nerves, doubt and persistence that come with trying to make it. That’s the heart of On My Way: before the breakthrough, there’s the road. The series captures the part we don’t usually see, when emerging artists are still figuring out what comes next. Khalid meets Ian and Bryce in that moment, offering perspective from someone who knows what it takes. By the end of each journey, an original song comes to life. For Ross, On My Way brings a new perspective, meeting Gen Z through something already central to their lives: music. Created with McKinney, the series moves beyond traditional advertising with 3 to 4 minute documentary style episodes about two young artists whose resourcefulness embodies everything Ross stands for today. The work continues beyond the series, with Ian and Bryce’s original songs released as full tracks available for streaming at launch. On My Way began rolling out with teasers beginning August 24 through OOH placements on college campuses across the country, followed by three trailers and full-length episodes beginning August 31 across Ross social channels including TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube. video_title: HubSpot — High Performers Perform Better With HubSpot
description: HUBSPOT GIVES HIGH PERFORMERS THE EDGE IN NEW GLOBAL CAMPAIGN WITH AKQA The best people at their jobs have something in common: they make it look easy. That ease isn’t accidental. HubSpot and AKQA today launch a new global brand campaign that puts those high performers front and center, and reveals that behind every effortless performance is HubSpot’s agentic customer platform. Built to connect marketing, sales, and service teams around a shared view of the customer, HubSpot brings together AI-powered tools and a Smart CRM, with customer data at the center. The campaign highlights how the platform helps businesses build demand, win deals, and delight customers. AKQA was tasked with developing a platform to move the brand beyond traditional B2B marketing conventions, putting the people using it at the centre of the story, highlighting the feeling that comes from having the right platform to excel. HubSpot appointed AKQA in March 2026 for its ability to unite brand, product, and customer experience through creativity. The campaign was produced through a highly collaborative model that kept creative, production, and post-production teams working in lockstep with HubSpot’s in-house brand and creative teams. Using the same director and production partner across shoots, with editors embedded on set, the team was able to lock cuts in real time and accelerate delivery without compromising quality. The teams partnered with acclaimed director Max Siedentopf and production company, DIVISION, to launch a series of teaser films set in quiet offices where HubSpot was already at work earlier this year. Today, the campaign introduces those people directly. Across a series of films, the workplace professionals are introduced - notable by their calm demeanour; prepared and in control, because they have the tools and information they need at the moment they need it. The full campaign includes a series of two teasers, five 30" brand films, four 15" product features films, and multiple audio spots and out-of-home activations across four markets (USA, UK, Australia, and Germany). “B2B marketing has spent years talking about itself. This campaign celebrates the people using the tools, the ones who are quietly, consistently excellent at their jobs. We built HubSpot to help every go-to-market team achieve more growth, and we wanted the world to see what that could look/feel like.” — Sunil Desai, SVP of Brand, HubSpot. “The creative idea started with a simple observation: the people who are best at their jobs often make it look effortless. We wanted to explore what sits behind that confidence and success. The campaign shows how the right insights, the right tools, and the right platform can help people perform at their best.” — Victor Davoine, Managing Director, AKQA Paris. description: Comic Relief, the nonprofit harnessing the power of comedy to drive action for kids facing poverty, launched a new large-scale national campaign today, built around a simple yet uncomfortable truth: it’s much easier to come up with reasons not to deal with childhood poverty than it is to actually do something about it. Introducing “Not Our Problem” – a fictional nonprofit “dedicated” to doing absolutely nothing about childhood poverty. The satirical hero film, directed by Brad Morris, takes aim at the absurd, everyday excuses people use to convince themselves that helping is someone else’s responsibility. Throughout the spot, a cast of ordinary people confidently explain why childhood poverty isn’t their concern, standing up to “take action” against standing up in the first place – culminating in a deadpan reveal that redirects viewers to real solutions. Developed in partnership with creative agency Quality Meats, the campaign represents a fresh departure from traditional cause advertising, using comedy to disarm, disrupt, and draw audiences into a serious issue in an unexpected way. Designed with a tone and relevance tailored for today’s cultural moment, the work directly confronts societal indifference by giving that apathy a name, a logo, and a satirical ad campaign of its own. “Not Our Problem” carries that central idea across a fully integrated national program: Turning the punchline into a point of entry: NotOurProblem.org, teased throughout the campaign, instantly redirects visitors to Comic Relief’s official site, turning the punchline into an actionable bridge from doing nothing to doing something. The landing page offers multiple pathways for people to get involved, whether by committing to one simple action a month right where they live, sharing the campaign spot across social media, or connecting with one of Comic Relief’s local Neighborhood Festivals. A dedicated Not Our Problem Instagram account extends the same deadpan, do-nothing energy (“Doing less. Together.”) across social media, with Comic Relief reposting the content through its own channels to create another accessible pathway for audiences to discover the campaign and connect with its mission. Using two voices to deliver one message: Out-of-home and print placements in the Not Our Problem voice lean fully into the satire (“1 in 6 children live in poverty, but ug ggghhhhh, can’t someone else help with that? Do nothing at NotOurProblem.org”), while corresponding Comic Relief branded messaging counters by turning the joke into a direct call to action (“‘Someone should do something about childhood poverty.’ How about you, person reading this?”). Marking Comic Relief's first dedicated, brand-focused national campaign, this campaign will extend from national reach into neighborhood action. The PSA will run as a fully integrated program across TV, out-of-home, print, and digital, including :60 and :30 anthem films with :15 cutdowns, an audio execution for music services, and organic social content to carry the message further. “Childhood poverty is a national problem happening in our own backyards, it is entirely solvable, and we can’t afford to wait any longer,” said Michele Ganeless, Chief Executive Officer of Comic Relief. “For too many of us, childhood poverty has been easy to ignore, and an almost acceptable fact of life. Comedy has the unique power to disarm people and say the truth in a way that gets heard and moves people to action, helping change the narrative from there’s nothing we can do about it to there’s something we can all do.” “Childhood poverty is definitely not funny. In fact it’s so painfully unfunny, that voluntarily doing nothing about it seems like a joke, said Brian Siedband Co-Founder and Co-CCO at Quality Meats. “And when you articulate the reasons why most people do nothing about it, when you proudly state it out loud, it sounds completely absurd. We’re using that absurdity as a Trojan horse to get people to question their own reasons for not doing anything.” As the campaign's own punchline puts it: It would be funnier if it wasn't so true. Beyond the national campaign, Comic Relief is bringing its call to action to life through Neighborhood Festivals, a new, nationwide series of free events launching this fall that make getting involved real, tangible, and simple. Kicking off on September 19 in Los Angeles at the historic Paramount Pictures Studio Lot, these in-real-life gatherings give people the opportunity to meet their neighbors and connect directly with local organizations working to end childhood poverty. The inaugural festival in LA pairs hands-on volunteering with entertainment, and will feature comedy performances from groups including The Groundlings and UCB. The campaign leans into comedy as a provocative force for change, reflecting Comic Relief’s unique ability to use humor to disrupt indifference and spark meaningful engagement. Rather than relying on traditional cause messaging, the work uses satire to disarm audiences, proving that comedy can move people from passive laughter to real-world action. This  professional campaign titled 'Not Our Problem' was published in United States in September, 2026. It was created for the brand: Comic Relief, by ad agency: Quality Meats. description: Just in time for the spooky season, M&M'S® is conjuring movie night magic to celebrate the theatrical release of Practical Magic 2, only in theaters September 10—the highly anticipated sequel to the 1998 Warner Bros. Pictures classic—with a limited-edition M&M'S Amas Veritas Spell & Snack Pack. "For generations, M&M'S have been a staple of Halloween celebrations and remain the perfect chocolate treat for every spooky moment throughout the season," said Allison Miazga-Bedrick, VP Marketing, Seasonal Portfolio, Mars Snacking. "With Practical Magic 2 coming to theaters, we wanted to give fans a fun new way to celebrate the magic of the season and bring friends together for a movie they've been waiting for. This partnership gives Practical Magic fans a nostalgic, colorful and spellbinding way to make their movie night even more memorable – with M&M'S along for the ride." Casting the "Amas Veritas" Spell In celebration of the new film, the M&M'S Amas Veritas Pack is inspired by the iconic scene in the heart of the original where young Sally Owens recites the "Amas Veritas" love spell—a charm that helps her envision the perfect, impossible man in hopes of protecting her heart. The pack brings the beloved film moment to life, allowing fans to recreate the magic bite-by-bite. Each pack features custom-designed M&M'S candies adorned with eight whimsical symbols inspired by the magical qualities of the spell. Bridging pure nostalgia with high-stakes anticipation for the upcoming theatrical sequel, the pack also debuts an "extended verse" featuring four brand-new symbols. These exclusive designs drop subtle hints about the mysteries brewing in Practical Magic 2. The limited-edition pack is available exclusively at MMS.com/Practical-Magic as a special gift with the purchase of M&M'S Milk Chocolate Fun Size Sharing Bag, a Halloween season-essential, while supplies last. In a playful nod to the film's iconic midnight theme, fans will have two chances to claim their pack during two exclusive drops at the stroke of midnight (12:00 AM ET) on: Drop 1: Thursday, September 3, 2026 Drop 2: Monday, September 14, 2026 A Spellbinding Partnership For fans who have spent decades waiting to step back into the Owens family's enchanting world, the long-awaited sequel Practical Magic 2 promises to deliver the ultimate dose of nostalgia with the return of sisterly bonds, playful shenanigans and whimsical magic. Now, in a way only M&M'S can, the brand is bringing that beloved cinematic heritage to life by reuniting fans with a familiar face from the original magic. M&M'S partnered with actress Camilla Belle, who famously played young Sally Owens in the original film. Nearly 28 years later, Belle will recite the famous "Amas Veritas" charm once again—this time with a signature M&M'S twist—in exclusive social content on Instagram and TikTok, inviting both lifelong fans and a new generation to fall in love with the franchise's magic. "Playing young Sally Owens in Practical Magic is still one of the most special memories from my early career, so coming back to this moment 28 years later has been such a nostalgic experience," said Camilla Belle. "Revisiting this beloved scene with M&M'S and giving the 'Amas Veritas' spell a sweet twist has been such a delight. I can't wait for fans to recreate the spell, share the fun on social and get excited for Practical Magic 2." description: Just days away from kicking off the 2026-2027 NFL season, Bud Light is making sure fans will always be able to rep their NFL team in style wherever they are this season. The Official Beer Sponsor of the NFL is bringing back its fan-favorite NFL team cans, created alongside Bud Light's 27 partner teams and featuring the iconic team logos and colorways. But every NFL season, fans across the league are unable to get access to their favorite team's can, whether they've moved out of their home team market or are traveling to rep their squad in a rival city. That's why this season, alongside its team cans, Bud Light is also introducing a new version of camouflage, where fans will be able to stand out with team pride wherever they are all season long. Can-O-Flage is Bud Light's latest innovation that will allow fans to transform any can into their team's Bud Light team can by simply slipping an insulated sleeve over any standard can. Whether hitting the stands at their home stadium, watching their team from the comfort of their friend's couch, or traveling to another city's tailgate, Can-O-Flage is available to fans 21+ across Bud Light's 27 team partners, so team pride comes first. Todd Allen, SVP of Marketing for Bud Light, said: "For years NFL fans across the country have asked us how they can purchase their team's Bud Light can if they don't live in that area. This season, we're excited to answer that call with Can-O-Flage. We're going great lengths to make sure that diehard fans 21+ can rep their squad wherever they are this NFL season. Our ongoing partnership with Fanatics allowed us to create this must-have game-day accessory so fans across the league can hit any away game, tailgate or watch party in style." Bud Light levels up NFL team cans with new Can-O-Flage. Bud Light is already getting fans 21+ gameday ready with the return of its iconic Bud Light NFL team cans, for 27 partner teams across the league. Featuring full-bleed team colors, retro-inspired jersey stripe marks and bold team logos to show off your team spirit, fans can make it clear where their fandom stands. This year's team cans also feature a scannable QR code that will give fans the chance to upgrade their gameday experience with prizes. But Bud Light knows that team loyalty has no boundaries, and fandom runs deep as fans go great lengths to support their squad throughout the NFL season. Ultimately, having your team colors and logo is key when cracking open a cold one on gameday. That's why the brand is introducing "Can-O-Flage" — an insulated sleeve that looks just like your favorite Bud Light team can — designed to keep your beer cold and allows you to always rep your team. It perfectly slips onto any standard can so fans can cheers to their team – even in opponent's territory. Available for purchase across the Fanatics network of sites, including Fanatics.com, NFLShop.com and select online team stores, as well as ShopBeerGear.com, Can-O-Flage is available now for $39.99 while supplies last. New social content puts Can-O-Flage in action. Bud Light is rolling out hilarious digital content featuring its all-star lineup of brand partners to help introduce the new Can-O-Flage innovation. Featuring Pro Football Hall of Famer Peyton Manning, comedian and actor Shane Gillis, and San Francisco 49ers star George Kittle, the brand released a series of new videos where the guys ensure they're repping their team on gameday: • Shane Gillis and George Kittle: The boys are posted up at the bar, grabbing a Bud Light when Shane is handed a 49ers can. That clearly doesn't match his Eagles fandom, so he smoothly pulls out his Can-O-Flage, designed for times just like these, so he can still rep the Birds. • George Kittle: When a buddy reaches out for a Titans team can, George promises he has the perfect thing and quickly intervenes to pass him the gold and red 49ers Can-O-Flage. • Peyton Manning: When Peyton is in the fridge looking to grab some Bud Lights, he is lost in the sea of team cans. Unsure what to grab, the legend pulls out his Colts and Broncos Can-O-Flage so he can still show his support for both teams as he enjoys the game. Peyton Manning, Pro Football Hall of Famer, said: "I personally appreciate Bud Light's Can-O-Flage so I can rep the Colts or the Broncos and get ready for gameday wherever I am this NFL season. It's another example of how Bud Light is always thinking about what they can do to turn up the fan game." George Kittle, San Francisco 49ers star, said: "The Faithful are the most dedicated fans out there and Bud Light's Can-O-Flage only amplifies that passion by bringing the excitement of the Bay to any stadium. Getting the chance to create some content with my buddy Shane was also a blast...even though he's an Eagles fan." video_title: Jones Coffee Roasters — All Grown Up
description: “All Grown Up” is the latest campaign for Jones Coffee Roasters and the second winning script resurrected through hungryman’s Dead Ad Society, an “anti-award show award show” created to give promising advertising ideas a second chance. The absurd premise follows a toddler who wants a sip of his mum’s coffee and, after being told it is only for grown-ups, somehow transforms himself into a fully grown man to get a taste. Written by Jagger Moore while at INNOCEAN USA and directed by hungryman’s Lena Beug, the idea was originally created years ago for a different coffee brand. Moore and his creative partner wrote dozens of scripts around the idea of the world’s best-tasting coffee, but another concept was chosen, leaving “All Grown Up” behind. Moore later submitted the forgotten script to Dead Ad Society’s second annual awards. From more than 250 submissions, the script became one of 16 finalists and was performed live by improv actors at The Mint in Los Angeles. A jury of leading creatives selected it as the night’s Gold winner, even though it had no client attached and existed only as a live performance. Less than a year later, the idea has been turned into a finished commercial for Jones Coffee Roasters. As part of the prize, hungryman provided full production with support from a group of industry partners, while INNOCEAN USA championed the winning idea and helped find a client to bring it to life. The collaboration came together in an unusual, almost backwards way, proving that a strong creative idea can survive for years and find its audience when the right people are willing to give it another chance. This  professional campaign titled 'All Grown Up' was published in United States in September, 2026. It was created for the brand: Jones Coffee Roasters, by ad agencies: Dead Ad Society and Hungry Man. description: Coca-Cola Thailand takes a hilarious look at workaholism in ‘The World Will Wait’ Ogilvy Singapore and Ogilvy Thailand bring a distinctly Thai sense of humour to Coca-Cola’s global campaign, directed by Wuthisak Anarnkaporn (Un). Coca-Cola Thailand is reminding people to put work aside and come back to the table with two new films for its global “The World Will Wait” campaign. Built around the importance of being present during mealtimes, the campaign celebrates the table as a place to switch off from work, distractions and everything else competing for our attention, and reconnect with the people around us. For Thailand, Coca-Cola takes a humorous look at the country’s famously hardworking culture. Across two films, “The Dentist” and “The Cable Guy,” work follows our protagonists all the way to the table, taking familiar occupations to increasingly hilarious extremes. The films are a collaboration between Ogilvy Singapore and Ogilvy Thailand, directed by legendary Thai filmmaker and Factory01 founder Wuthisak Anarnkaporn (Un), who brings his unmistakable comedic storytelling and visual wit to the work. Komkrib Chockchaikatanyu, IMX Director of Creative / Content, Coca-Cola Thailand, said: “Today, work doesn’t end when we leave the office. There’s always another email, call or distraction asking for our attention. Coca-Cola has always been part of the moments that bring people together, and ‘The World Will Wait’ is a reminder to put work aside, share a meal and a Coke, and be present with the people around us.” Nikhil Panjwani, Executive Creative Director, Ogilvy Singapore, added: “Thailand takes work seriously, so we thought we shouldn’t. We took the very familiar idea of bringing work home and took it somewhere outlandish. Un was the perfect mastermind to bring it to life in his inimitable Thai way.” This  professional campaign titled 'The World Will Wait' was published in Singapore and Thailand in September, 2026. It was created for the brand: Coca-Cola, by ad agencies: Ogilvy Singapore and Ogilvy Thailand. This Film medium campaign is related to the Drinks (Non Alcoholic) industry and contains 2 media assets. description: IShowSpeed and Dr. Squatch have teamed up for SPEEDRUN: Million Dollar Mission, a nine-week campaign offering fans the chance to win a share of a $1 million prize pool. Running from August 31 through October 31 across the U.S., Canada, the UK and Australia, the campaign features 25 challenges inspired by IShowSpeed’s unpredictable personality, with Walmart locations and select retail partners serving as participation hubs. The challenges are designed to be deliberately ridiculous, asking fans to complete tasks such as racing strangers, performing strange public stunts or even barking at a Dr. Squatch display in a store. Participants must film their attempts and post them to TikTok, Instagram or YouTube while tagging Dr. Squatch to qualify. Fans can also hunt for special briefcases containing prizes worth up to $50,000 in cash, with clues released throughout the campaign. Another $250,000 is being distributed through 25 $10,000 scratchers included in specially marked IShowSpeed Loot Box Bundles on TikTok Shop, while fans can also request a scratcher for free through the campaign website. The campaign will conclude with a final hunt worth another $250,000, although the details have yet to be revealed. Rather than relying on a traditional sweepstakes, SPEEDRUN turns the giveaway into a chaotic combination of social challenges, scavenger hunts and real-world participation, giving IShowSpeed’s fans plenty of opportunities to compete, create content and potentially win big. This  professional campaign titled 'Million Dollar Mission' was published in Australia, United Kingdom, and United States in September, 2026. video_title: The Link School of Business — Against the Current
description: The Link School of Business, Brazil’s only university fully dedicated to entrepreneurship, announces its arrival in Miami, becoming the first Brazilian educational institution to establish operations in the United States. The move marks a new chapter for the institution and for Brazilian entrepreneurial education, bringing to the U.S. a teaching model designed to develop entrepreneurs capable of building global businesses from day one. The choice of Miami reinforces Link’s internationalization strategy. Recognized as one of the world’s leading hubs for innovation, technology, and entrepreneurship, the city brings students and companies closer to an international business ecosystem while expanding opportunities for connections between Brazil and the United States. To communicate this milestone to the market, agency ANONIMA.ag and production company Not Brand have created a film that translates Link’s The Founders College spirit into a story about courage, ambition, and the ability to create one’s own path. Produced using artificial intelligence while preserving the realism of the marine environment, and featuring an original soundtrack by Satélite Áudio, the film follows the journey of a fish that decides to leave its enormous school and venture alone into the unknown. Along the way, the protagonist faces obstacles that mirror the challenges of entrepreneurship: fear, judgment from others, market resistance, wrong turns, crises of confidence, and the need to push beyond one’s own limits. After overcoming countless challenges, the fish finally reaches its destination. The film’s concept captures the meaning behind this journey: Entrepreneurs don’t follow markets. They create markets. “A story like this, told in this way, would have been incredibly difficult to produce within the same timeframe and constraints without artificial intelligence,” says Amanda Talli, founder and director at Not Brand. “Building an entire underwater world and following a sardine as the protagonist would traditionally require a massive production, potentially combining underwater filming, 3D, and multiple techniques. AI allowed us to bring an idea of this scale to life in just a few weeks. At the same time, we were telling a deeply human story, created so that so many entrepreneurs could see themselves in it. That meant the technology could never overshadow the connection we wanted the story to create. Our goal was for it to disappear entirely, leaving only the story behind. And that’s where craft became essential: every decision in cinematography, direction, and visual world-building had to serve the narrative. The ocean needed to feel as beautiful as entrepreneurship often looks from the outside, while, for those who have actually built something of their own, every element needed to reflect the emotions and challenges that only someone who has lived through that experience would recognize.” Fabio Mozeli, co-CEO and Chief Creative Officer of ANONIMA.ag, explains: “While traditional universities prepare executives to enter existing markets, Link prepares people to create new ones. That insight gave rise to Against the Tide, a human metaphor for the courage to forge your own path. Inspired by the behavior of large schools of fish, the film follows a sardine that chooses to answer its inner calling and discover what lies beyond the familiar current. The result is a cinematic story that combines realism, exceptional craft and emotion to capture the essence of Link: empowering entrepreneurs to forge their own paths and make way for what’s next — now in one of the world’s leading business hubs,” says the campaign’s creative lead. Running across digital channels and social media in Brazil and the United States, the campaign marks Link’s arrival in Miami and brings its Global from Day One positioning to life, reinforcing its internationalization strategy and its mission to develop entrepreneurs prepared to create opportunities, connect markets, and generate global impact. “Link’s arrival in Miami represents an important step in our internationalization strategy and reinforces our mission to develop entrepreneurs prepared to build businesses with a global vision from day one. This campaign captures exactly that spirit of having the courage to explore new markets and turn opportunities into impact,” concludes Álvaro Schocair, CEO of Link School of Business. This  professional campaign titled 'Against the Current' was published in Brazil and United States in September, 2026. description: Clash of Clans*, which has over two billion lifetime downloads, is back with WWE for a second collaboration; and this time, the rivalry is personal. WWE Superstar Cody Rhodes and WWE Legend John Cena are best known for what they do in the ring, but their competition didn't start there. Both are long-time players of Clash of Clans, and this shared gaming history has become locker room legend. Now, Rhodes, a decade-long player, has recruited the Clash of Clans community – plus fellow WWE Superstars – to help him hunt down John Cena's base, taking a decade-long battle out of the ring and into their in-game villages. Beginning today, September 1st, through September 30th, Cena’s loot-filled base is waiting for Clash of Clans players to discover throughout the course of their daily raids. The more players raid, the higher the chance they have of locating the elusive WWE Legend and earning a one-time-only Cody Rhodes statue for their village – but only if their raid is a success. It’s not like a 17-time WWE World Champion is going to have a rookie base. Meanwhile, to beef up the search party, Rhodes has enlisted the support of The Undertaker, IYO SKY and a whole host of other WWE Superstars who will be rallying their own fans online to join the hunt. “People think this started in the ring with Cody. It didn’t. It started when I out-raided him in the game and he threw me off his team," says Cena. “Ten years later he still needs help. This time he’s asking millions of you to take on my base. That’s fine. As I have always said - if you want some, come get some.” Beyond Cena’s base, the in-game crossover presents six WWE Superstars reimagined as iconic Clash of Clans Hero characters, including the return of Cody Rhodes as The Barbarian King. The lineup include: Cody Rhodes as “Barbarian King” Alexa Bliss as “Archer Queen” The Undertaker as “Grand Warden” IYO SKY as “Royal Champion” Jey Uso as “Minion Prince” Kane as “Dragon Duke” Players can also experience WWE-themed features throughout the event, from temporary troops to a branded village theme that’s designed around WWE Money in the Bank, taking place in New Orleans on October 10th. WWE chests hold a series of rewards too, with returning favorites like Action Figure Equipment, Challenge Tickets and a guaranteed Cody Rhodes Skin**. Download Clash of Clans for iOS or Google Play today to help Rhodes in his Search for Cena until September 30th. description: Arla unveils Feed Life™ as ‘Breakfast Yourself to Victory’ kicks off new creative chapter New masterbrand platform Feed Life™ provides long-term strategic direction for Arla marketing First campaign, Breakfast Yourself to Victory, uses humour and cultural insight to reconnect Britain with breakfast – created by Droga5 Integrated work spans TV, social, influencer, experiential and OOH Arla Foods UK has unveiled Feed Life™, its new long-term masterbrand platform, alongside the launch of Breakfast Yourself to Victory, an integrated campaign created by Droga5 London that aims to put breakfast back at the centre of Britain's busy mornings. The launch marks a significant step in Arla's masterbrand strategy, moving beyond awareness-building activity towards creating stronger emotional and cultural relevance for the Arla brand across its portfolio, which includes Arla Cravendale, Arla Protein and Arla Skyr. Feed Life™ will provide the strategic framework for how Arla connects its products, purpose and marketing activity through a single promise: enabling good food choices that make life better. The platform is designed to create stronger meaning for the Arla masterbrand while helping consumers see the role nutritious dairy can play in everyday life. Danny Micklethwaite, VP Marketing at Arla Foods UK, said: "Over the last year we've worked to build greater visibility for the Arla masterbrand. The next challenge is building stronger meaning and relevance. “Feed Life™ gives us a long-term strategic platform that connects our products, our portfolio and the role we can play in helping people make better food choices. "Breakfast Yourself to Victory is the first major creative expression of that platform. It's rooted in a genuine cultural tension, delivered with humour, and designed to show how better food choices can help people win life's little internal competitions every day." The integrated campaign, developed with Droga5 London, will run across television, digital, social, influencer, experiential and out-of-home channels. The campaign films have been brought to life by award-winning director Jeff Low starting from the simple observation that we all secretly get a kick out of winning life’s little competitions, and that breakfast can be your unfair advantage. Tara Ford, Chief Creative Officer of Droga5 London, said: "Breakfast is simple. Winning is fun. Bringing the two together gives us a big, joyful idea that can go anywhere. Simple, silly and full of energy." Breakfast Yourself to Victory represents the first chapter of Feed Life™ in the UK, with future activity set to extend the platform across additional consumer, brand and cultural territories. This  professional campaign titled 'Breakfast Yourself to Victory' was published in United Kingdom in September, 2026. It was created for the brand: Arla, by ad agency: Droga5 London. This Film, Integrated, and OOH Outdoor media campaign is related to the Food and Retail Services industries and contains 4 media assets. It was submitted 31 minutes ago.

description: State Farm’s latest football campaign, created with Highdive, uses football, humour and personalised storytelling to demonstrate why insurance should be as individual as the people it covers. The campaign builds on the brand’s long-running idea that having insurance is not the same as having State Farm, putting a sharper focus on what makes its coverage personal. The campaign brings together familiar names including Patrick Mahomes and Andy Reid with emerging talent such as Cam Skattebo and Fernando Mendoza. Rather than using a single creative formula across its talent partners, each story is tailored to the personality, interests and circumstances of its subjects while reinforcing the central idea that coverage is personal. The campaign includes several distinct spots. In “Getting to Know You,” Jake from State Farm spends the day with Skattebo, exploring his unusual habits and energetic personality. “For Ashley” reunites Mahomes and Reid in a spot built around Ashley’s interests, including football and dogs, while “For Mike” uses Mahomes to show how personal preferences should extend to insurance coverage. “Power Stance” features Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti bringing his signature sideline pose to a CBS co-branded spot with Jake from State Farm. The 360-degree football campaign was developed with High Dive and supported by Optimum Sports, STN, Pretzl, Infinity Marketing Team, OMD and FleishmanHillard. By giving each talent and story its own creative treatment, State Farm turns personalisation into something audiences can see and experience rather than simply a claim from the brand. This  professional campaign titled 'Having Insurance Is Not the Same as Having State Farm' was published in United States in September, 2026. It was created for the brand: State Farm, by ad agency: Highdive. This Film medium campaign is related to the Insurance industry and contains 4 media assets. It was submitted about 8 hours ago.

description: Premium yoghurt brand The Collective has launched its month-long TV debut, “The Dairy Shaker-Uppers”, created, planned and bought by Bountiful Cow. Marking a step change in brand investment, the activity is The Collective’s first masterbrand TV campaign, taking its adult and kids ranges to a national audience for the first time. The spot opens like an anonymous hacker video: grainy footage shot in a darkened room, the silhouette of a hooded figure barely visible as a distorted voice announces: “We are The Collective… the dairy shaker-uppers.” But when the voice distortion glitches and the lights come on, the mysterious figure is revealed to be a perfectly ordinary mum in a pink hoodie – who happens to take her yoghurt very, very seriously. Armed with a child’s voice-altering microphone she can’t quite get to work and, more importantly, an unwavering devotion to truly epic yoghurt, she attempts to deliver an impassioned manifesto anonymously from the comfort of her spare room. As family life gradually interrupts her mission, the ad reveals the everyday reality behind the brand’s fanatical commitment to flavour, fruit and creaminess. Eventually recruiting her two sons to the cause, the spot culminates in the playful rallying cry: “The revolution is coming… and it will be served chilled.” The film captures The Collective’s irreverent spirit and premium credentials in equal measure, celebrating the joy, chaos and authenticity of family life while reinforcing the brand’s position as “the dairy shaker-uppers” who refuse to compromise on taste. The campaign marks a clear evolution in The Collective’s brand strategy, building a distinctive brand world obsessed with taste and their loyal following, whilst maintaining the brand’s insight-led, irreverent and humorous approach. Having expanded beyond OOH and social with its first AV activity in cinema earlier this year. The Collective is using its first foray into TV to continue subverting the conventions of the dairy category and invite consumers to join the revolution. The media strategy is designed to give the challenger brand disproportionate impact. Bountiful Cow has concentrated TV investment exclusively with Channel 4 across linear and VOD, creating greater presence and unlocking added value rather than spreading budget across multiple broadcasters. Meta and YouTube will extend the campaign digitally, while the continuing cinema activity will overlap with the TV launch. Running nationally around the key back-to-school period, the campaign also takes The Collective beyond its traditional London heartland to reach new audiences across the UK. Amy Bellchambers, Marketing Director at The Collective, said: “This is a huge milestone moment for the brand as we launch onto TV for the first time and take consumers’ love of our brand to a national stage. We’re a bold and disruptive scale-up brand, and it’s amazing to be able to bring that to life through a compelling, ownable creative territory and highly impactful media plan that will really drive our long-term brand awareness building journey.” Adam Foley, CEO at Bountiful Cow, said: “The Collective has always behaved like a challenger, so its TV debut couldn't look or feel like conventional dairy advertising. This is about taking the personality that has made the brand distinctive and giving it a much bigger stage. By bringing creative and media together, we’ve been able to build the idea and the plan around the same ambition - concentrating investment with Channel 4, supported by cinema and digital, to create disproportionate impact and take The Collective’s revolution nationwide.” This  professional campaign titled 'The Dairy Shaker-Uppers' was published in United Kingdom in September, 2026. description: Guide Dogs has launched an integrated campaign to show the impact it has on the lives of people living with a vision impairment through its breadth of services. Developed by Fold7, the work highlights the ways Guide Dogs helps people with vision impairment live the lives they choose, independently, confidently and without limits. To bring this to life in an emotionally compelling and relevant way, the campaign taps into a universal feeling that everyone can relate to – the sense of achievement when you overcome a barrier or master a skill for the first time. Every day, all over the UK, people with sight loss are doing something for the first time. Small moments to some, but for people living with sight loss, they are enormous triumphs. Most of us will never understand what it’s like to live with sight loss, but we all recognise that feeling. The launch campaign shows how the charity works with people with sight loss across the UK to help them achieve their significant life ‘firsts’. Sitting at the heart of the campaign is a two-minute hero film called “First Steps” directed by BAFTA award winning Director Tom Green at Stink UK and voiced by Maxine Peake. Known for his emotive, character-driven, and cinematic style, Green often works with real people rather than actors. The film’s cast consists of Guide Dogs service users from all different ages, backgrounds, and stages of sight loss. Drawn from their own life experience, we see them overcome personal challenges and feel their pride when they achieve their significant “firsts”: a teenager going to school with friends for the first time after losing their sight. A football fan returning to his familiar place in the stands, now with his guide dog. A toddler mastering her cane for the first time. The film ends with the line “Your donation helps make life-changing firsts possible for people with sight loss.” Dave Billing, Executive Creative Director at Fold7 said: “Sighted society is too often ignorant of the challenges of living with sight loss, or aware of the amazing stories of people with vision impairment overcoming those challenges, every day. Tom Green was the perfect director to tell those stories, by working with real people with sight loss rather than actors and gently drawing out their experiences to make the film carry real emotional weight and truth. It's a piece of work with real heart, that I hope makes people more aware of the realities of sight loss and the incredible work that Guide Dogs does.” The integrated campaign is also running in Print, Social and Radio. The social campaign, “Behind Every First”, goes behind the scenes of the vignettes seen in the TVC, showing the partnership between service users and Guide Dogs specialists as they work together to overcome each person’s individual challenges. Meanwhile, radio spots feature people with visual impairment leaving voice notes for the Guide Dogs team members that have helped them. As part of the agency remit, Fold7Design, the design studio within Fold7, expanded Guide Dog’s visual identity for comms, including a new bespoke font that was developed with vision impairment in mind, which features in the campaign. The campaign introduces a new long-term creative platform developed by Fold7 – “Life Unleashed’ – which future proofs the brand with a unifying creative expression for fuelling growth and audience engagement. On the creative platform, Terry McGrath, Chief Fundraising and Marketing Officer at Guide Dogs, adds: “Life Unleashed represents a shift in how we want people to understand Guide Dogs’ mission; it’s about removing the barriers that stand in the way of people living the life they choose. This first campaign from our new creative platform reframes perceptions and repositions Guide Dogs as the dynamic, forward-thinking organisation we are today and will be in the future.” The brand premieres on 28th August and will run until the end of September, with Legacy advertising also developed by Fold7, running until the end of October. description: Astral Tequila, the official tequila partner of Warner Bros. Pictures' highly anticipated Practical Magic 2 and featured on-screen in the film, is bringing its bright and crisp tequila to the franchise’s iconic cocktail tradition with the Astral Midnight Margarita and “It’s Midnight Somewhere,” an original five-part social microdrama starring real-life sisters, models, and television personalities Brooks and Grace Ann Nader. Created in partnership with the production company Merman and directed by Madelaine Turner inspired by the mystery, magic, and sisterhood of Practical Magic 2, the series follows the sisters as a night of making Astral Midnight Margaritas turns into an unexpected adventure filled with humor, surprises, and sisterly shenanigans. All five episodes are now LIVE on Astral’s YouTube Shorts channel. "Microdramas are a very effective format for brand storytelling, and this project is the type of brand-inspired entertainment that Merman specializes in," said Kira Carstensen, Global Managing Director at Merman. "Astral Tequila, and the upcoming film Practical Magic 2, are integrated into the story and made a key part of the narrative. You might say there is ‘magic’ in the microdrama method; it is as much a piece of entertainment as it is brand messaging. We loved working with Astral Tequila, Hunter PR and Warner Brothers and applaud them for taking this adventurous approach." “Creatively, the microdrama format gave us room to really play,” said Turner. “We established characters and a world and gave audiences a reason to come back for the next episode. That episodic structure also gave us more opportunities to build Astral into the heart of the story. The sisters have that playful push-and-pull — they tease each other, they have completely different personalities, but there’s always that underlying closeness. That felt like such a natural fit for a story built around sisterhood and connection, and around those moments of getting together, making an Astral Midnight Margarita and seeing where the night takes you.” "The 'Midnight Margaritas' tradition embodies the same energy that's at the heart of Astral Tequila: the best nights are made brighter by the people you share them with, especially with an Astral Midnight Margarita in-hand," said Jenn Rapp, Director, Portfolio Tequila & Mezcal at Diageo North America. "With its agave-forward, citrus profile, Astral brightens every cocktail, making it the perfect tequila for moments of connection." Madelaine Turner is a Los Angeles-based writer, director, and content creator who revels in the visual medium and loves storytelling in all forms. Madelaine’s self-made viral videos – sitting at the intersection of period aesthetic and modern pop culture – have garnered millions of views and likes. With over 480K followers and counting on TikTok, her creativity has led to collaborations with high-profile brands such as Adobe, Gucci, PlayStation, Dolby and more. As a commercial director, Madelaine has brought her social-first creator mindset to large-scale campaigns for brands like Target, Walmart and Home Goods. All five episodes of the “It’s Midnight Somewhere” will roll out across Astral Tequila’s YouTube Shorts, Instagram and TikTok beginning August 26. Microdramas are one of social media’s fastest-growing formats for storytelling, captivating audiences with bite-sized episodes, dramatic cliffhangers, and binge-worthy narratives. While the format continues to gain momentum, only a handful of brands have tapped into its potential to connect with younger audiences in the way they’re already consuming content. This  professional campaign titled 'It’s Midnight Somewhere' was published in United States in August, 2026. It was created for the brand: Astral Tequila, by ad agency: Merman. description: Part of the daily life and consumption of both Brazilians and Americans, discount coupons attract the public as an alternative to pay less on selected products and to pay off debts. Based on this behavior, Serasa – a credit platform focused on improving perople’s financial health - creates its unprecedented campaign, starring Tichina Arnold, known for playing Rochelle in the series Everybody Hates Chris. Recorded in Hollywood and developed in partnership with Oliver Latin America through Pinkers, the in-house agency dedicated to Serasa, the production connects references to the financial universe to show that this alternative is a great ally in debt negotiation. In the film, the actress travels to Brazil and is enchanted by the experiences and products she finds along the way. The passion for the country soon turns into a passion for spending until she realizes that the bills have started to accumulate, bringing out the strong personality and complicated relationship with money already known to the public. However, the arrival of Boletinho, Serasa's mascot, brings a solution to the problem: a coupon that offers a discount on the negotiation of debts. "The series remains present in the imagination of Brazilians, bringing that nostalgia and affection for the characters, in addition to a certain identification with the situations experienced by many families, especially when we look at financial difficulties and the need to save. This humor, which manages to transform everyday situations into lightness, is something that speaks a lot to the way Serasa has communicated with people", comments Renan Maximiano, creative director at Serasa. "When we thought about a campaign about coupons, it made a lot of sense to look for someone who represented this strong culture in the United States. At the same time, we wanted a personality who had a genuine connection with Brazilians. Tichina brings together these two attributes in a unique way: in addition to coming from a market where the use of coupons is part of people's routine, she is widely recognized and loved in Brazil for her role in the series, a striking maternal figure that crossed generations. This combination allowed Serasa to build a narrative with cultural relevance, nostalgia and a lot of identification with the public", highlights Beto Rando, business director at Oliver. A production that crosses borders The campaign marks an unprecedented moment in Serasa's history: it is the first time that the company has recorded an advertising production outside Brazil. Filming took place in Hollywood, at Sunset Las Palmas, a studio owned by Disney, which has already hosted productions such as I Love Lucy, The Fat and the Skinny, The Addams Family and La La Land. With humor and identification, the project expands the way of presenting Serasa coupons, showing that they can not only help in the shopping economy, but also as allies when negotiating debts, making room for financial organization. The campaign also has the participation of the official voice actors of the series: Guilene Conte, who voices Tichina Arnold and the character Rochelle, and Philippe Maia, responsible for the voice of Chris Rock and the narration of the series. "The project was born from a combination of elements that talk very well to each other. In it, we were able to connect pop culture, the financial universe and Serasa in a spontaneous way, using humor, nostalgia and identification to bring the brand closer to Brazilians and talk about a financial product in a light way", reinforces Renan. With a strong appeal among the Brazilian public, the campaign also reaches Serasa's social networks, which will publish financial education pills recorded with the American actress. The content brings advice related to personal finance, with the touch of good humor characteristic of Tichina Arnold and her character. Complementing the promotion, the brand will also have influencers such as Lore Rufino, Lúcio Sincero and Álvaro, to amplify the message, and will carry out a seeding strategy, which will include sending a perfume "Puro Cupom" to selected content creators and engaged followers. The treat takes advantage of the campaign's motto and uses nostalgia, linked to one of the remarkable episodes of the 2005 series. This  professional campaign titled 'Everybody Loves Coupons' was published in Brazil and United States in August, 2026. It was created for the brand: Serasa, by ad agencies: In-house Serasa and Oliver. This Film medium campaign is related to the Finance industry and contains 1 media asset. It was submitted 1 day ago.

description: Accessible fashion is stuck between two extremes. Online giants are flooding closets with volume over vision, and legacy competitors are chasing high-fashion runway collabs that feel out of reach for everyday women. maurices, a value fashion retailer with a 95-year history serving hometown communities across America, is taking a different approach with its first major brand campaign for fall. As part of a comprehensive 2026 brand refresh designed to capture new customers and re-engage their core demographic, the effort puts its biggest differentiator center stage: making real, personal styling accessible without the luxury price tag (or luxury markup). Something the brand has been doing for 95 years. The integrated campaign also marks the first major campaign launch from Art of Something, an independent creative agency founded in 2025 by industry veterans Rob Kurfehs (ex-BBDO, Publicis) and Dan Sormani (ex-Goodby Silverstein & Partners, Mother), along with Head of Strategy Kat Logan (ex-Saatchi & Saatchi, Johannes Leonardo). Art of Something built maurices’ debut campaign around a phrase that usually signals privilege: "I have a stylist." Here, it means something different — at maurices, having a stylist isn't a luxury, it's "just a regular Tuesday”. Kristine Koetter, CMO at maurices commented:  “What people may not know about maurices is that every woman can walk into one of our stores and receive personal styling for free. Our associates have an incredible ability to help women discover what works for them, feel confident in their style, and even try something unexpected. This campaign shines a light on what makes maurices truly different: creating a place where women can discover clothes they love, put them together with confidence, and ultimately feel like the best version of themselves.” Rob Kurfehs, Creative Director, Founder at Art of Something commented: “It’s a rare opportunity when you have a brand partner that has a compelling differentiator—and is down to lean into comedy to attract new customers to the brand. The vision for these was always for them to feel less like ads and more like little pieces of prestige TV.” This  professional campaign titled 'Sophie Has a Stylist' was published in United States in August, 2026. It was created for the brand: maurices, by ad agency: Art of Something. This Film and Integrated media campaign is related to the Fashion industry and contains 1 media asset. video_title: Caleb McDuff Motorsport — Fuelled by Silence
description: Disability turns into a competitive advantage for an 18-year-old Welsh racing driver in a new film from TheGardening.Club and Hijinks, created through its Positivity Through Creativity programme. Caleb McDuff, who was diagnosed as profoundly deaf in early childhood, is aiming to secure new brand sponsorships through the campaign, ‘Fuelled by Silence’. Directed by Lee J Ford through The Gardening.Club, the 90-second film uses AI to transport McDuff and his car from familiar racing circuits to the remote reaches of the universe – a place that mimics his deaf driving experience. Narrated by McDuff, the film traces his journey from learning to drive as a child to competing professionally. We discover how, unable to use in-car radio systems available to other competitors, McDuff raced in silence and learned to harness it to his advantage. Archive footage of McDuff’s childhood racing exploits is blended with AI-generated imagery that places him and his car driving on spectacular remote planets, places where silence reigns. The film reveals that technology now enables him to communicate with his team during races, and we end with McDuff saying: “Now I am ready to prove to the world just how loud silence can be.” Aged 16, McDuff became the first deaf racing driver to win a race in the Britcar Trophy Championship. Now McDuff needs to secure more sponsorship to ensure he reaches his goal of competing in the Porsche Carrera World Cup 2027. Caleb McDuff said: “I never let being deaf stop me. This film tells my story and shows that when you believe in yourself, you can overcome any barrier. My message to everyone is to always follow your dreams. My message to potential sponsors is that I’m only just getting started.” The campaign was developed through Hijinks’ Positivity Through Creativity programme, set up to serve pro bono clients. Work through the programme has also included campaigns for Women’s Aid, Legalitees and WeRepresent. Tamryn Kerr, co-founder and chief creative officer at Hijinks, said: “The starting point wasn’t that Caleb succeeds despite the silence, but that the silence helped make him the driver he is. We wanted potential sponsors to see his extraordinary talent, focus and ambition, and understand just how far he has the potential to go”. “AI allowed us to bring that idea to life on a scale that would never otherwise have been possible for a pro bono project. Used with imagination and purpose, it helped us give Caleb’s story the platform and breadth of recognition it deserves.” Morgan Whitlock, Executive Producer at TheGardening.Club adds: “From the moment I met Caleb and his team I knew we’d do everything we could to support them. Everyone on this project has brought that same passion and commitment, it’s been a phenomenal process and that shows in the film the team have created. If it moves the needle for Caleb, it’ll have been worth every moment.” The film breaks today on social, online video, press and Caleb McDuff Motorsport’s website, with plans for out-of-home and cinema activity in discussion. This  professional campaign titled 'Fuelled by Silence' was published in United Kingdom in August, 2026. It was created for the brand: Caleb McDuff Motorsport, by ad agencies: Hijinks and The Gardening Club. This Film medium campaign is related to the Sports industry and contains 1 media asset. video_title: First Interstate Bank — No Nonsense Banking
description: TDA Boulder has unveiled “No Nonsense Banking,” its debut campaign for new client First Interstate Bank. The rolling launch runs through the end of the year, and spans across 10 states. This marks the independent agency’s first work for the Billings, Montana headquarter-based bank, which is the primary subsidiary of First Interstate BancSystem, Inc. About the campaign: The work is built around a simple idea: people don’t have patience for nonsense, and neither does First Interstate Bank. Rather than reinventing banking, the creative positions the brand as bringing banking back to the basics: straight answers, human relationships, and tools that work. The campaign includes audio, CTV, digital display, high-impact rich media, out-of-home, social, and search. The creative is anchored by the hero spot, “Every Step,” with accompanying spots “Actor,” “Handshake,” and “Keys” carrying the same point of view. “Every Step” opens on a couple experiencing life’s biggest moments (marriage proposal, first child, learning to drive, and packing up for college), capturing meaningful moments with one odd addition: their banker is actually really there, experiencing those moments with them. The unexpected inclusion calls out the cliché that banks love to be with you every step of the way, even in life’s most intimate moments. The spot lands on the twist: First Interstate isn’t promising to be there for every step; just the ones that matter, with a straight answer and a real person on the other end. The media mix extends to out-of-home in places most major banks skip entirely. TDA Boulder’s “Middle of Nowhere” boards show up in towns that might feel remote to some but are exactly where First Interstate has long done business, with headlines including “The only B.S. out here comes from cattle,” “Because banking should be out in the open,” and “Out here, nonsense doesn’t last long.” This  professional campaign titled 'No Nonsense Banking' was published in United States in August, 2026. It was created for the brand: First Interstate Bank, by ad agency: TDA_Boulder. This Film and Integrated media campaign is related to the Finance industry and contains 4 media assets. description: SAME WORDS, DIFFERENT WORLDS: EIGHT ARTISTS WORKING WITH AI REIMAGINE A SCRIPT BY OSCAR-NOMINATED EFTHIMIS FILIPPOU Oscar-nominated screenwriter Efthimis Filippou, behind The Lobster, The Killing of a Sacred Deer and Kinds of Kindness, collaborates with MikeTeevee on a new experiment in AI filmmaking What happens when eight artists are given the same script, access to AI filmmaking tools and complete creative freedom? The project began with an original scene written by Oscar-nominated screenwriter Efthimis Filippou, whose
