description: Disruptive performance footwear brand R.A.D® (Rally Against Destruction), has moved into skateboarding footwear through a campaign with longtime creative partners, FLUORO®. The R.A.D® MANNY ONE represents a raw fusion of high-performance skate functionality and 90s retro-futuristic street style. Engineered alongside skateboarding legend Manny Santiago, the shoe is built to handle high impacts and long sessions without sacrificing comfort, boardfeel or style. The challenge for launch was to communicate the shoe’s innovative features in a way that feels authentic to both R.A.D® and Manny Santiago. The launch campaign presents an expressive, expansive brand world that is more entertainment than advertising. It channels Manny’s relentless optimism and DIY spirit within a retro-futuristic aesthetic that borrows from early gaming and draws on diverse references, from Japanese animation to carnival masks reflecting the skater’s Puerto Rican heritage. Ephemera, texture, tone and motion come together in a highly distinctive realm that plays out across touchpoints. Brand launch film The launch film is an absurd take on an epic wipeout. It’s a wild ride that brings the brand feeling to life with a mix of real-life footage, innovative animation and moving image. Set in a London, the film sees Manny Santiago turbo-charged skywards, running through a series of personas. In anime style he endures the ascent only to be eaten by a dragon, then morphs into a plasticine figure which deconstructs to a skull, then just a brain, eyeballs and spinal cord. He falls to earth as a game character, making explosive impact with the ground back in filmed footage mode, embedded in a hole in the ground with comedy wonky limbs. The camera pulls in on his signature tooth gap, which sprouts an exposed nerve that becomes the ‘A’ of the R.A.D® logo, while he laughs in the background. Texture, tone and energy The teaser campaign featured pixelated GIFs of the R.A.D® logo and logotype, with go-faster stripes coming across like old Commodore games loading. Embedding tech in a more tangible world brings distinctive texture and tone. Unchained from the narrative conventions of advertising, FLUORO® was freed to home in on texture and materiality, pace and rhythm, unlocking the euphoria of skateboarding. Playful performance FLUORO® and R.A.D® have worked together to communicate the MANNY ONE performance credentials within a street skating context, through a digital launch rollout, showcasing tantalising glimpses of the shoe’s design. A graphical rendering of the heel-to-toe drop shows the feel underfoot; the swell foam gets stamped on and bounces back into shape; the TPU heel clip spins in space; the madly durable printed toe cap is envisioned as a beast; and the rubber sole bends in a colourful, textural representation of flexibility. Blended brand and advertising Dialling up the colour and exuberance, the R.A.D® MANNY ONE campaign is built, like the shoe, to appeal across ages and genders, with skaters at the core. Creative elements, unchained from marketing conventions, are orchestrated as an entire, distinctive brand world. FLUORO® achieved this through its signature holistic approach that blends the lasting impact of branding with the commercial urgency of advertising, so that both work harder together. This  professional campaign titled 'MANNY ONE launch' was published in Multinational Europe, United Kingdom, and United States in August, 2026. It was created for the brand: R.A.D®, by ad agency: FLUORO®. This Content, Digital, and Film media campaign is related to the Fashion, Fitness, and Sportswear industries and contains 6 media assets. description: College move-in day: a harrowing rite of passage. Graduate by Hilton's new back-to-school campaign, created with social-first creative agency Movers+Shakers, turns one of the year’s most chaotic family moments into an orientation for the fictional Order of the Stay, a not-so-secret club that makes college move-in more manageable. The hero spot plays like an initiation video, complete with an oath and a narrator, played by actor, writer & social media influencer, Clayton Farris, (@claytonfarris4ever) who guides viewers through the Graduate experience while introducing the very-real absurdities of college move-in day, from exhausted parents to students confronting the reality of leaving home. The creative also pulls directly from the Graduate by Hilton brand. Its hotels are designed around the college towns they call home, with school-specific references, local history, and unexpected design details woven throughout each property. The campaign will run across the brand’s social channels, supported by additional short-form spots. Graduate is also extending the idea through a creator program featuring different perspectives on the college experience, from a senior reflecting on move-in day to a design-focused creator exploring Graduate’s interiors and a parent recreating the move-in experience. description: Making the new Wake Forest University 30-second TV commercial started with cutting nearly 3,000 pieces of paper into campus landmarks, trees and people. Every element was designed, engineered, and assembled by hand. The commercial is scheduled to air for the first time during the Sept. 3 Wake Forest football game and will continue to air throughout the season. Building a Wake Forest world out of paper and then filming it had a purpose: highlighting Wake Forest’s commitment to developing leaders of character and integrity. “At Wake Forest, character formation is an area of intense academic study and gets incorporated into curricular and co-curricular activities,” said Vice President for University Marketing and Communications Brett Eaton. “I love that this commercial highlights the University's leadership of a national character development movement in a creative and thoughtful way. It also speaks to the student journey and the community of care that makes it meaningful.” A website (wake.wfu.edu/commercial) with a behind-the-scenes documentary tells the full story of the idea, the process of making it and the people involved. description: A new epic creative spot for Audi's fully electric e-tron range celebrates quiet confidence as a powerful asset, steering the e-tron away from the category norms back to Audi's core sporting DNA. 'After Dark' is a cinematic, mischievous spectacle that returns Audi to its ancestral home: the race track. BBH London playfully draws on Audi's decades of motorsport engineering to show how technologies born in the thrilling, high-octane world of motorsport, including instant acceleration, quattro precision handling and intelligent braking, have been tamed for the road. Shot at the legendary Silverstone Grand Prix Circuit, where Audi is the official car partner, the 90 second slot, directed by Elliott Power via Love Song, features four Audi e-tron models carrying out a coordinated mission. Rather than driving like ordinary cars, they move with purpose and instinct, each expressing its own personality through choreography inspired by its unique strengths. They evade the security guard and dog as well as skilfully avoiding the mechanic at work. By the end of the film, the cars have made their way to the Silverstone starting grid, where we leave them ready for the real fun to start. Proof that the e-tron range captures Audi's Vorsprung durch Technik DNA of pushing the boundaries of performance. Tony Moore, Head of Marketing at Audi UK, said: "The Audi e-tron range combines advanced electric performance with the engineering heritage and innovation Audi is celebrated for. Vorsprung durch Technik has always been about using the craft of design and engineering to move people, and today that philosophy is embodied in our electric vehicles. This campaign captures that beautifully, showing that our e-tron range is every bit as exhilarating, capable and innovative." To underline Audi's heritage in the motorsport space, the film also features a cameo appearance by the Audi R18 e-tron quattro, a hybrid model, which won the 24 Hours of Le Mans three years running from 2012 to 2014, a clear reminder of how far back Audi has been innovating in the EV space. description: Stink Studios has created a new brand campaign for Raylo, a subscription service for phones, laptops, tablets, consoles and other electronics. It is the brand’s first TV campaign in several years and Stink Studios’ first work for Raylo after winning the business through a competitive pitch. The campaign highlights how quickly technology becomes outdated, comparing upgrading devices to modern dating. Rather than committing to a device that may soon feel old, Raylo’s subscription model allows customers to move on to something newer and better when the time comes. Stink Studios’ creative team similarly draws a parallel between keeping technology and relationships casual, suggesting that subscribing makes it easier to move on when something better comes along. description: How American Haiku Used AI to Bring a 16-Year-Old Film Featuring John Hurt to Life A short film over a decade in the making is finally seeing the light of day, powered by technologies that didn’t exist when it began. Awful Dreams, a short film from full-service creative ad agency American Haiku, combines a long-abandoned script by the shop’s founder and CCO, Thom Glover, with a previously unheard voice performance from Sir John Hurt, recorded in 2010 and left dormant for nearly sixteen years. Originally conceived as a practical-effects horror in the vein of John Carpenter’s The Thing and Alien, the project stalled after repeated funding setbacks. The script, written as a gothic poem in blank verse, tells the story of a butcher plagued by a nightmare in which the animals he has slaughtered return as a single, grotesque entity, hellbent on his demise. Despite early momentum and Hurt’s involvement, the film was never produced. The materials were eventually shelved, including the actor’s recorded narration. That changed in 2024, when Glover connected with director and AI artist Michael Hess. Rather than revisiting the project as originally intended, the pair chose to rebuild it using generative AI tools, embracing early versions of the medium’s unpredictability as a creative asset to generate disturbing imagery. Where many AI-driven films aim for realism, Awful Dreams leans into the technology’s tendency toward distortion and hallucinations. Bodies shift unnaturally. Forms blur and collapse. The imagery resists coherence, creating a sense of unease that aligns closely with the film’s premise. Hurt’s voice anchors the piece, adding weight to a production that bridges multiple timelines. The actor, who died in 2017, never saw the finished work. His performance, recorded for a version of the film that was never made, now exists within a project shaped by new tools and techniques. That tension sits at the center of Awful Dreams. It is both archival and experimental, human and machine-made. At a time when AI in filmmaking is often framed around efficiency or replacement, American Haiku’s approach suggests a different path. Instead of smoothing over flaws, the film uses them to heighten its central idea, drawing on the discomfort that comes from images that feel neither fully alive nor entirely artificial. The project, which has had significant success on the festival circuit, where it attracted attention not only for its use of AI, but for the unusual circumstances of its creation. QUOTES “Awful Dreams is a project we tried to get off the ground in multiple different ways for many years” said Thom Glover, Founder and CCO of American Haiku and writer behind Awful Dreams, “but it found its true expression in the nightmareish qualities of early AI models”. “Most AI films are trying to show how close the technology can get to reality. We were much more interested in where it breaks,” said Michael Hess, Director of Awful Dreams. “There’s something deeply unsettling about imagery that almost makes sense but doesn’t quite resolve. That tension became the visual language of the film.” “This project sits at the intersection of old and new in a way you rarely see. A script from 2010, a performance from Sir John Hurt, and a production process that only became possible recently,” said Mateo Suarez, Executive Producer of Awful Dreams. “For us, it’s less about what AI replaces and more about what it enables. This is exactly the kind of idea that benefits from that shift.” This  NSFW  professional campaign titled 'Awful Dreams' was published in United States in August, 2026. campaign_hint: If It’s Not Right Guard, It’s Wrong Guard
video_title: Right Guard — If It’s Not Right Guard, It’s Wrong Guard
description: Right Guard is launching “If It’s Not Right Guard, It’s Wrong Guard,” a new campaign created in collaboration with Party Land that recasts every competing product in the deodorant aisle as “Wrong Guard.” In a category where absurdity has become a familiar playbook and brands often compete to be the weirdest in the room, Right Guard’s campaign is deliberately simple. It puts the product, name, and efficacy message at the center, using plainspoken, unpretentious humor to make the comparison easy to understand and hard to forget. The “If It’s Not Right Guard, It’s Wrong Guard” campaign marks Party Land’s first work for the brand since winning the assignment in a competitive national pitch against four other agencies. Created for an audience of hard-working men who want a deodorant that works as hard as they do, the campaign treats sweat protection as a practical decision. It gives Right Guard a clear way to drive reconsideration and trial among a younger generation while staying rooted in the brand’s sweat-protection promise. The work builds on Right Guard’s “For Men Who Sweat” positioning with a broader platform designed to close the awareness gap with younger men and establish Right Guard as their go-to antiperspirant. “Right Guard has over six decades of brand equity, including a long history of using humor to connect with consumers. That heritage translates to very high awareness among older consumers, but almost nonexistent awareness among 18-24 year-olds,” said Peter Olson, Senior Director of Marketing, Thriving Brands. “In a category dominated by global conglomerates and high-spending startups, we knew we couldn’t just buy our way into relevance. We needed an ownable idea that could earn relevance and keep working for Right Guard over time. We collaborated with Party Land to build something simple, confident, and unexpected. ‘If It’s Not Right Guard, It’s Wrong Guard’ puts our product promise first and gives us a platform we can continue to build. "I love it when a brand has the confidence to take on a whole category. It gives us the permission to not only come out swinging, but also make the right work instead of the expected work," said Matt Heath, co-founder and chief creative officer at Party Land. For Party Land, the campaign reflects a belief that humor works best when it makes the product message clearer. The campaign’s writing carries that approach across five spots, with lines including, “Wrong Guard, bad. Right Guard, right,” and “Do not hire Wrong Guard. It’s so expensive. Instead, hire Right Guard.” In another spot, the voiceover says, “A working man’s life is blood, sweat and tears. But if that working man uses Right Guard, it will just be blood and tears.” The national campaign is running across streaming TV, online video, digital, social and Reddit. This  professional campaign titled 'If It’s Not Right Guard, It’s Wrong Guard' was published in United States in August, 2026. It was created for the brand: Right Guard, by ad agency: Party Land. video_title: Paddy Power — Why the Football Not?
description: After a huge World Cup this summer, Paddy Power is getting audiences excited for the incoming football season with the launch of its brand new football-focused brand platform, 'Why The Football Not?' created by BBH London. From the sublime to the ridiculous, the platform celebrates the sheer unadulterated absurdity of British football fandom. It focuses on the weird and wonderful experiences and behaviours that make the game great, to get fans asking, "Why the football not?" The hero film stars national treasure Danny Dyer, who has now been the star of several PP campaigns, and former England striker Peter Crouch both answering and asking a series of questions, to which there can only ever be one real answer. When asked by a naysayer in the pub, 'why do you even care?' about football, Danny gets thinking… What follows is a whirlwind tour through some of the beautiful game's most baffling behaviours, as he contemplates the 'why'. From over-the-top matchday fancy dress to ick-inducing bedrooms obsessively decorated in club colours and a new father proudly celebrating the birth of his baby daughter, Jurgen. In a typically hilarious cameo, Peter Crouch asks a suspicious onlooker why he's filming another team's training session, in a cheeky nod to a former club's Spygate scandal. The only real answer to the clueless bystander's question? "Why the football not?" Leah Spears, Marketing Director at Paddy Power said: "From Spygate to Danny Murphy's cat Bob being a breakout star of the World Cup, we live and breathe football at Paddy Power. So, after the longest season ever, the biggest World Cup of all-time and another England heartbreak, some people might wonder why we're going again. English football is the greatest game on Earth, so we say, why the football not?" Paddy Power ambassador Danny Dyer said: "Football's a funny old game, and us fans can be a strange bunch. One minute you're absolutely losing your head, saying you're done with it, the next you're hugging your mates and kissing some random bald geezer right on his dome. It doesn't make any sense, but that's why we love it." Peter Crouch added: "Football fans are great because we're all a little bit ridiculous, in the best possible way. That's usually where the magic comes from and leads to all those silly moments on and off the pitch. You don't really need a good reason to care; you just love it anyway." Packed with viral memes, football in-jokes and Easter eggs for eagle-eyed fans, the campaign follows Paddy Power's huge World Cup activity this summer and is designed to get fans fired up for the new 2026/27 season, kicking off on 21st August. The film was shot at Brentford FC stadium and directed by Max Barden via Anonymous, who also directed the World Cup spot for Paddy Power starring Rob Lowe alongside Dyer. The campaign will launch on 19th August across the UK and Republic of Ireland for at least the next nine months. Media was handled by EssenceMediacom. This  professional campaign titled 'Why the Football Not?' was published in Ireland and United Kingdom in August, 2026. It was created for the brand: Paddy Power, by ad agency: BBH London. video_title: Formation Games — Football shaped thoughts and feelings on football club owners and other football things
description: Think you could run a football club better? New creative by independent games studio Formation Games and Ace of Hearts for CLUB game, dares the nation to prove it. Starring a returning Jeff Stelling, the show brings to life every fan’s belief that they could manage a football club better than the owners. In "Football shaped thoughts and feelings on football club owners and other football things”, Stelling tracks down football's loudest voices and puts their opinions back to them, inviting the fans with the strongest views on club ownership to prove they could do better. Jeff Stelling, commented: “We’re yet to see how the 2026/27 season plays out, but pre-season hasn’t disappointed - big transfers, new managers, and boardroom drama! The question is, could you do a better job of running a football club? That’s what we’re putting to the test with Club Game, where fans can prove if they can run a club better!!”. For a long time Jeff has been the presenter fans built their Saturdays around, and his return to screens has landed as expected. Teased on his own X channel last week, here, the teaser garnered 1.5M views in the first day, and featured top in Trending. The show already has fans counting down to his comeback, with reactions including: "This is where you belong. Wherever you are, I'll be watching like I was for almost 30 years." "Jeff Stelling might have single-handedly saved 2026. 💪😍" Every football fan has an opinion on their club's owners. People certain they'd have managed their club better, from manager appointments to the players that should never have been sold. Formation Games and Ace of Hearts have decided to take them up on it, offering Formation Games’ free-to-play game, CLUB, as the place they can step into an owner's shoes. The new format sees Stelling popping up unexpectedly around the country to hear fans' hottest opinions. From there the series turns reactive, seeking out supporters with particularly strong views on how their clubs are run and putting them on the spot. CLUB goes beyond the standard fantasy football framework. Fans build their dream club from their phone, taking control of stadium upgrades, managing transfers and loans, investing in backroom staff and designing the club crest, with their side scoring points based on real players' performances. Football ownership has never been more of a talking point, from Wrexham's Hollywood fairytale to KSI's recent involvement at Dagenham & Redbridge, which CLUB sponsors this season. CLUB simply gives fans at home the chance to have a go themselves. Throughout the Premier League and after, Ace of Hearts and Formation Games will keep the conversation running, reporting back on fans' thoughts and feelings on club ownership through a steady stream of content across social and contextual OOH. description: JCPenney’s new campaign “Retail Rejuvenation,” which treats bad shopping habits like an illness, was produced by Good Behavior and directed by Pete Marquis. The four-minute film follows six shoppers at a Retail Rejuvenation Retreat to start healing those bad shopping habits – from clothing cleanses to mindset mantras – and see the light at JCPenney. The campaign highlights a recent JCPenney survey that found 88%  of discount shoppers said it’s actually easy to shop at JCPenney, 76% said they find what they came for – in their size – and 77% already feel that peace of mind when they walk through our doors. * Another 87% of budget conscious customers agreed their “visit to JCPenney is worth my time,” and 92% confidently said, “I got a good deal” at JCPenney. “Here’s what we know about you,” said Marisa Thalberg, executive vice president, chief customer and marketing officer for Catalyst Brands. “You don’t want less. description: For leaders of growing mid-sized companies, ambition is a given. What's not is having technology that can keep up with where the business is trying to go. These companies are competing with larger players with deeper resources, scaling quickly, and need to make technology decisions with little room for error. Their current systems may be reaching a breaking point, but replacing them can feel like a slow, expensive disruption they cannot afford. And many assume SAP is built only for global giants. That tension sits at the center of SAP’s new GROW campaign, created in collaboration with BBDO New York, which turns the potential of growth into a series of visual metaphors: one workspace stretches and reconfigures while another instantly adds to its workforce as each business expands. Directed by Rupert Sanders, the work dramatizes the pressure and possibility of growth, showing companies gaining flexibility, momentum and sustainable growth through technology. The production uses practical effects, a deliberate choice to keep the story grounded in the real experience and mindset of the audience. “Rather than starting with cloud ERP capabilities, we started with a feeling every growing business leader understands: the pressure that comes when your business outgrows the way it’s been operating. That human insight became the foundation for the entire campaign because people connect with challenges before they connect with solutions," said Ada Agrait, Global CMO, SAP. While much of the enterprise technology category talks about automating the work, SAP’s GROW campaign focuses on automating growth: helping business leaders scale without fighting against systems that no longer fit. GROW is designed specifically for ambitious mid-sized businesses that need AI cloud ERP built to move with them, not slow them down. GROW is SAP's entry point to cloud ERP, and delivers a complete, AI-enabled platform for finance, supply chain, and HR, with preconfigured industry best practices embedded from day one. [link] "Growing a business takes guts. It always has. Every new stage brings bigger opportunities, bigger decisions, and bigger expectations. That's the idea behind SAP GROW. For more than 50 years, SAP has helped businesses navigate those moments of change, and today we're helping the next generation of companies grow with the confidence to keep building what's next," said Ray Page, Chief Brand & Creative Officer, SAP. For SAP, the story connects to a larger brand strategy around confidence in change. Across its 50+ year history, SAP has helped businesses navigate major technology shifts. GROW applies that idea to fast-growing mid-sized companies, showing that enterprise-grade systems are not just for giants, but for companies with giant ambition. The campaign is running on CTV, LinkedIn Social, YouTube and Google Video across North America, Italy, Germany, Japan. "When we walked onto set and saw the level of craft that went into this project, into building what’s probably the tiniest office in the world, and combined that with the human craft that developed the technology we were communicating, that’s when it all came together for us. Human ingenuity on both sides," said Kleber Menzes, SVP Group Creative Director, BBDO New York This  professional campaign titled 'GROW' was published in United States in August, 2026. video_title: Eli Lilly & Company — A Life Covered
description: For many people, obesity is a lifelong struggle. As we age, health becomes increasingly important to enjoying the years we've saved for, sacrificed for and earned. In partnership with Wieden+Kennedy Portland, today, Lilly debuted its latest campaign, "A Life Covered," which marks a milestone: Lilly obesity medicine is now covered through the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge program for eligible Medicare Part D beneficiaries. "A Life Covered" advances Lilly's effort to challenge category norms and bring conversations about the lived experience of obesity into cultural spaces. As Lilly's fourth major campaign addressing longstanding assumptions and stigma around obesity, it builds on a broader creative platform reshaping how obesity is represented and understood. Anchored by a flagship film, the campaign tells a deeply personal story about living with obesity across a lifetime and how access to medicine offers hope for the future. Weaving together memories, photographs and artifacts, the film illustrates the lasting burden of obesity while reflecting an experience shared by millions. The work reinforces Lilly’s belief that putting health above all means fighting to make medicine more accessible for those who need it. description: The dust has settled, the turf is down, and the gates have officially opened. Carhartt, America's premium workwear brand, has once again partnered with the Buffalo Bills as they prepare to kick off their next era at the newly completed Highmark Stadium. To mark the occasion, Carhartt is shining a spotlight on the hardworking people behind-the-scenes who built the new Buffalo stage, as well as the tradespeople nationwide who supply the game's essential elements. This work comes together in the next chapter of Carhartt's creative brand campaign, Made Possible, which honors the tradespeople whose hard work shapes some of our beloved and iconic shared experiences. In the first chapter of the Made Possible campaign, which launched in August 2025, Carhartt highlighted the early stages of Highmark Stadium's construction through the story of Bills legendary running back Thurman Thomas and his commercial construction company, 34 Group Inc., which was responsible for installing the seats in the new stadium. This fall, the campaign picks up where that story left off, with Thurman showcasing the dedication, craftsmanship and pride of his crew and the thousands of hardworking people who helped bring the stadium to life by giving current Bills star running back James Cook III his first tour of the state-of-the-art venue. "Stadiums aren't just concrete and steel, they are monuments to what can happen when grit, skill, and purpose come together," said Norma Delaney, Vice President of Marketing and Brand Creative at Carhartt. "This season, we are proud to stand alongside Bills legend and construction leader Thurman Thomas, and current Bills running back James Cook III to honor the hardworking crews whose contributions are often overlooked but are critical to every game-day experience. From the first shovel in the ground to the opening kickoff, major construction projects like the new Highmark Stadium are made possible by hardworking people wearing Carhartt." The campaign is anchored by a 30-second hero spot, "Making Football Possible," which is a unique, reverse-look from finish to start, beginning with the fans cheering, rewinding to the seats being installed, the sod being rolled, the uprights going in, and the footballs being created, because it takes a collective effort of hardworking skilled tradespeople to make game day possible. While the campaign is anchored in Buffalo, this fall's installment expands its lens to celebrate the workforce behind stadiums nationwide that support football year-round – from the sod to the uprights. The campaign also includes two-minute longform, behind-the-scenes videos: • Constructing Highmark Stadium alongside Thurman Thomas and his crew at 34 Group Inc. • Carolina Green, the family-owned farm serving as one of the major natural grass suppliers for NFL stadiums across the country. • Aluminum Athletic Equipment (AAE) and the skilled welders behind the uprights that define the end zone in multiple NFL stadiums. This multi-year campaign celebrates the physical completion of Highmark Stadium while honoring the grit of the thousands of men and women who bring the game to life. "It's an honor to take the field in this new stadium, but we know none of this happens without the crews who actually built the stage we play on," said James Cook III, Buffalo Bills Running Back. "Partnering with Carhartt and Thurman to officially pass the torch and thank the workers behind the scenes is the perfect way to kick off this exciting new chapter for Bills fans." Additionally, when the Bills take the Highmark Stadium field for their first preseason home game on Saturday, Aug. 15, Carhartt will thank the hardworking people who brought the new stadium to life with a Rally Towel giveaway for the first 20,000 fans in attendance. The Rally Towels will be printed on the front and back and will feature the names of every person on the crews who worked on the new stadium. Carhartt will also run messaging in-stadium during the Bills preseason games to pay tribute to the crews. This  professional campaign titled 'Made Possible' was published in United States in August, 2026. It was created for the brand: Carhartt, by ad agency: Unreasonable Studios. description: Brandon and Avelo Airlines Launch “If You Know, You Avelo,” Repositioning Regional Airports as the Smarter Way to Fly The agency's first work as creative and media AOR launches across five origin markets Brandon, named creative and media agency of record for Avelo Airlines in May 2026, has launched “If You Know, You Avelo,” a new campaign that introduces travelers to the convenience of nearby regional airports and encourages them to rethink how they fly. The campaign began rolling out in late June, with digital ads going live June 26 and additional placements following the week of June 29. Video and radio elements are set to launch upon completion. The campaign is built to shift the long-held assumption that larger airports are the only option. It positions Avelo as the simpler, more convenient choice and is designed to drive awareness and consideration among net-new travelers who have not yet flown with the airline. At the center of the creative is the idea of being let in on a secret. A paper airplane serves as the campaign's guiding visual metaphor, representing the simplicity and joy of travel before it gets swept up in the chaos of a crowded airport, only to reappear in the calm of a welcoming regional one. The storytelling leans on nostalgia and a sense of magic to reinforce the brand's promise. Rather than exaggerated claims, the messaging highlights tangible benefits travelers can expect from flying Avelo: nearby, convenient regional airports; lower parking costs; faster security lines; nonstop flights; competitive fares; and access to destinations many travelers didn't realize were within reach. The work rolled out across five bases — Charlotte / Concord, NC; Dallas / McKinney, TX; Philadelphia / Wilmington, DE; Orlando / Lakeland, FL; and New Haven, CT — with localized creative for each. The campaign ran through a full-funnel media mix including paid social on Meta and TikTok, YouTube pre-roll, display, digital audio, CTV/OTV, digital billboards, and high school athletic partnerships. Media placements included iHeart streaming and podcasts targeting listeners in priority zip codes, Audacy streaming and in-game professional sports (MLB and NFL), Cadent, and YouTube. Creative was tailored by market, with each of the five markets receiving its own display units, dedicated TikTok and Meta executions in both subtle and heavier localizations, and shared :30 and :15 video spots and a radio spot. “We all have that friend who always seems to know the better way to fly,” said Austin Scott, Chief Creative Officer at Brandon. “A lot of the time, it's not even the airline — it's the airport. Avelo flies nonstop, exclusively out of regional airports, so parking is easy and the lines are short. It's the best-kept secret in travel, and 'If You Know, You Avelo' is our way of letting people in on it.” This  professional campaign titled 'Repositioning Regional Airports as the Smarter Way to Fly' was published in United States in August, 2026. It was created for the brand: Avelo Airlines, by ad agency: Brandon. This Film medium campaign is related to the Travel and Tourism industry and contains 1 media asset. It was submitted 1 day ago.

description: Grey London, as part of WPP’s team Vitale, has launched a new campaign for Parodontax built around the message ‘Spitting Blood Means Action.’ Directed by Finn Keenan through Riff Raff Films, the campaign uses the visual language and spectacle of martial arts cinema to challenge conventional healthcare advertising and raise awareness that bleeding gums can be a sign that action is needed. The 90-second film begins with an ordinary tooth-brushing routine before quickly turning into an action sequence when the protagonist notices blood in the sink. She races to a pharmacy and becomes involved in a highly choreographed battle over the last tube of Parodontax, using toothbrushes as weapons and dental floss as a lasso. The concept plays on the familiar movie trope where characters shrug off blood and carry on, reframing that behaviour to show how people often dismiss bleeding gums in real life. Launching across EMEA through 2026 and 2027, the campaign targets health-conscious adults who take an active approach to their wellbeing but may not recognise when specialist gum care is needed. With nearly half of adults expected to experience gum disease at some point, the work aims to make Parodontax the memorable choice for people experiencing gum problems by replacing the clinical tone of traditional dental advertising with humour, action and high-energy storytelling. description: Magners has unveiled a cheeky new mural on Brighton Street, Edinburgh, marking its ongoing sponsorship of Underbelly; one of the largest comedy venues at the world's biggest arts festival. Magners is its official cider partner. Created by creative agency ARK, the mural continues the 'That's Magnertism' platform, which launched in May 2025 and has driven Magners' broader UK marketing since. Rather than the polished, product-glorifying imagery typically associated with drinks brands, Magners opted for something rawer and more irreverent - betting that comedy fans queuing for Underbelly's stages will get the joke instantly, without it being over-explained. The partnership sits within Magners' wider sponsorship of Underbelly, which sees the brand's Original Irish Cider, 0.0%, and Dark Fruit poured across 13 venues throughout the festival, alongside a dedicated Magners Bar in George Square. It follows the launch of Magners' "Share The Craic" search for new stand-up talent, which culminates in a funded run at Underbelly's Wee Coo at this year's Fringe. As part of summer plans, Magners will also return to TV screens with its That’s Magnertism commercial - created by ARK in May 2025 - that conveys the contagiously positive feeling that the first thirst-quenching gulp of Magners brings. This will be complemented by outdoor advertising that lets the liquid do the talking with macro shots of Magners that highlight the refreshing choice Magners and the wider category offers during the summer months. Xander Hart, Creative Partner, ARK Agency, said: "Drinks advertising is obsessed with looking good, with someone loving what's in the glass. We wanted to do the opposite. There's something honest about a spit-take: it's the biggest compliment comedy can get. We knew comedy fans queuing outside Underbelly would clock that immediately, and we loved that Magners was brave enough to let us show their product being spat out" . Phoebe Small, Head of Brand, Magners, said: "The Fringe has this brilliant, unpredictable energy. Anything can happen on stage, and the audience is right there with it. We wanted our sponsorship to have that same spirit rather than just putting our name on a wall. Magners has always been about spontaneity and good craic, so poking fun at ourselves felt like the most honest way to show up at the world's biggest arts festival." Marina Dixon, Underbelly's Head of Programming, said: "The Edinburgh Festival Fringe is where so many great comedy careers begin, and many have been launched on Underbelly stages. We're passionate about helping new talent find their audience. Through 'Share The Craic', we're excited to support the next wave of comedians with mentoring and guidance, alongside the opportunity to bring their show to Underbelly at the Edinburgh Fringe and take that all-important next step in their career." The mural went live on Brighton Street, Edinburgh, on 11th August 2026, and will remain in place for the duration of the Edinburgh Festival Fringe, which runs until 31st August 2026. This  professional campaign titled 'That's Magnertism' was published in United Kingdom in August, 2026. It was created for the brand: Magners, by ad agency: ARK Agency. description: Bud Light has launched a new national campaign for the upcoming NFL season, created by Anomaly NY and directed by Damien Shatford through Biscuit. Starring Shane Gillis and Peyton Manning, the campaign features two commercials, ‘The Move’ and ‘Armchair’, built around the lengths fans will go to secure a Bud Light during gameday. ‘The Move’ takes place in a crowded bar, where Gillis and Manning compete for the bartender’s attention before Manning recruits a fan to help him stretch across the bar and place their order. In ‘Armchair’, Manning faces a different gameday dilemma at a watch party when he needs another Bud Light but refuses to surrender his prime seat, ultimately carrying his oversized recliner with him, even crashing through French doors. The campaign also brings back Bud Light’s limited-edition team cans in partnership with all 27 NFL team partners. Featuring retro-inspired designs, the cans include QR codes giving fans 21+ the chance to win gameday upgrades such as NFL+ Premium, tailgating essentials and NFL tickets. The campaign celebrates the passion of NFL fans while extending Bud Light’s long-running connection with the sport. description: Cuisinart has launched ‘A Work of Cuisinart: The Roommates,’ its first episodic social campaign created specifically for TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube Shorts. Developed by Fallon, the 14-part non-linear series moves away from traditional product-focused advertising, using dialogue-driven humour and entertainment-first storytelling to connect with younger audiences while showcasing Cuisinart’s kitchen innovations. The series follows Lucy, a passionate modern home cook, and Bruno, a literal starving artist transported from the 17th-century Baroque era who immediately recognises culinary craftsmanship. Together, the unlikely roommates demonstrate how the right kitchen tools can turn everyday cooking into an art form, with six Cuisinart products featured as they create everything from roasted chicken to homemade ice cream. Directed by Kelsey Taylor with food styling by Sue Li, the campaign builds on Cuisinart’s ‘A Work of Cuisinart’ platform by positioning cooking as a creative outlet rather than a chore. The social-first format is designed around the way audiences naturally consume short-form content, combining theatrical humour and product demonstrations to show how home cooks can turn everyday ingredients into culinary masterpieces. This  professional campaign titled 'A Work of Cuisinart' was published in United States in August, 2026. It was created for the brand: Cuisinart, by ad agency: Fallon. video_title: Tesco — Know What You're Sitting On
description: Timed to coincide with the school summer holidays, Tesco’s latest campaign from BBH London encourages customers to see their weekly shop as the gateway to getting away; whether on holiday, out for dinner or for a family day out. ‘Know what you’re sitting on’ shines a light on one of Clubcard's best kept secrets: the rewards customers could already be enjoying Tesco found that half a million of its Clubcard members are sitting on at least £100 to use with its Reward Partners. So, they decided to depict the scale of these discounts in a very literal way in a new campaign, running on TV and OOH as part of the ‘Need anything from Tesco?’ brand platform. The three films each focus on a different kind of Clubcard Reward. From a mountain of inflatables and sun umbrellas representing travel and holidays, to dining tables and chairs for restaurants and nights out, and a rollercoaster, for those family moments. Instead of creating these mountains of objects in post-production, the team, working with directors Glue Society, via Biscuit Filmworks, opted to build the sets from scratch, to demonstrate, in very real terms, the breadth of value Clubcard members could unlock. Murray Bisschop, UK Marketing Director at Tesco, said: “We know how easy it is for customers to focus on the great value that Clubcard Prices deliver and not notice their points and vouchers mounting up. We wanted to remind Clubcard members that the vouchers they are sitting on could be turned into big savings on holidays, meals out or days out. BBH have come up with a fun and engaging campaign that really brings that message to life for Tesco shoppers.” Gary McCreadie, Creative Director at BBH London, said: “It’s so easy to tap your Clubcard and not think about what you might be missing. This campaign captures the scale of Tesco discounts in a very real, dramatic, and hopefully unforgettable, way.” Each film points audiences to the Tesco app, with some of its well-known Reward Partners, including Hotels.com, PizzaExpress and Alton Towers Resort, shown on screen. The campaign is running on TV, VOD, DOOH, radio/audio and digital display in the UK. This  professional campaign titled 'Know What You're Sitting On' was published in United Kingdom in August, 2026. It was created for the brand: Tesco, by ad agency: BBH London. This Film and OOH Outdoor media campaign is related to the Retail Services industry and contains 8 media assets. description: Cornett Launches ‘Bluegrass Bathing’ for Lexington Tourism VisitLEX invites visitors to for a “grounding” wellness experience they can only get in Lexington, KY on the “best ground in the world” Wellness seekers are spending thousands on retreats, cold plunges, and longevity supplements. Lexington, Kentucky has a simpler suggestion: touch grass. Specifically, Bluegrass. In collaboration with long-time partner Cornett, VisitLEX, the Lexington Convention and Visitors Bureau, today launches Bluegrass Bathing, a new destination-wide wellness experience that invites locals and visitors to kick off their shoes, settle into Lexington's iconic Bluegrass landscape and reconnect with nature. The concept draws inspiration from the growing popularity of “grounding,” also known as “earthing,” a wellness practice centered on making direct contact with the Earth's surface, allowing the body to absorb its natural electrical charge. According to recent medical reports, this connection can help improve sleep, lower stress levels, and reduce inflammation. “You can sit on the ground anywhere. But there’s something special about sitting on the same earth that nourishes the world’s best Thoroughbreds,” said Jonathon Spalding, Group Creative Director at Cornett. “Why touch regular boring grass when you can touch Bluegrass?” As the Horse Capital of the World, visitors are surrounded by more than 450 horse farms. Set among the rolling hills and lush green spaces that define Kentucky's Bluegrass Region, Bluegrass Bathing transforms one of Lexington's most recognizable natural assets into an immersive wellness experience. "If grounding is all about reconnecting with the Earth, then we're inviting folks to start their wellness journey with the best, most natural and nutrient-rich ground in America," said Mary Quinn Ramer, President of VisitLEX. "For centuries, these rolling hills have nurtured some of the world's most celebrated Thoroughbreds and the limestone water that runs beneath it has become the bedrock of our bourbon industry. But it’s also the way this Bluegrass makes you feel. Visitors consistently report they feel more relaxed the moment they touch down in Lexington. Bluegrass Bathing is our invitation to slow down, take a breath and experience the landscape that makes Lexington unlike anywhere else in the world." Visitors can “Bluegrass Bathe” at some of Lexington’s most iconic outdoor spaces, including a selection of Visit Horse Country farms and a handful of Lexington’s scenic parks (including Kentucky Horse Park, Gatton Park, and designated Parks & Rec locations). By booking at participating locations, guests will receive access to a series of curated wellness experiences including Pilates and sound baths along with a selection of guided meditations designed specifically for the program. Additionally, guests can deepen their connection to the Bluegrass by booking a dedicated tour of their host farm after the bathing experience. Each of the guided meditations was inspired by the natural elements that shape Lexington's landscape, encouraging participants to slow down, engage their senses and connect with their surroundings. VisitLEX has also produced a guided Sound Bath video set amidst a local horse farm and led by Amy Hudson, a certified Reiki master and sound healer from the Sound Healing Center of Lexington. To celebrate the launch, VisitLEX has also released a promotional video inspired by luxury wellness retreats. The video follows a solitary Bluegrass Bather enjoying a lush field of Bluegrass while a soothing narrator extols the virtues of one of Kentucky's most abundant natural resources. "We love creating experiences that could only happen in Lexington," added Ramer. "Bluegrass Bathing playfully reminds travelers that sometimes the best reset is simply being present and reconnecting our bodies with the Earth in a beautiful, natural setting. It's wellness, Kentucky-style." Visitors can learn more about Bluegrass Bathing at VisitLEX.com/Bluegrass-Bathing, where they can access all of the guided meditations, explore participating locations and discover additional wellness experiences throughout the destination. This  professional campaign titled '‘Bluegrass Bathing’ for Lexington Tourism' was published in United States in August, 2026. It was created for the brand: VisitLEX, by ad agency: CORNETT. description: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/6QmcgkSszZc Booksy and Humanaut Help Dallas Beauty Pros Bring Pet Portraits to Life at Sit. Stay. Style. Booksy has teamed up with creative agency partner Humanaut to host a live, pop-up pet studio in Dallas that shows how the booking app helps beauty and wellness providers build and grow thriving businesses – regardless of their focus or area of expertise. To bring that brand promise to life, the global beauty booking app tapped Humanaut to help it create Dallas’s most specific beauty studio. Called “Sit. Stay. Style.,” the one-day pop-up event took place in Dallas’s Deep Ellum neighborhood and featured local beauty and creative service professionals who treated guests to hair, nail, and tattoo art services that were inspired by their pets. Prior to the event, Humanaut created a short teaser video and static social assets, which Booksy used to drive awareness and fill bookings. One teaser encouraged local pet parents to book an appointment for “your pet’s portrait on you.” Four participating beauty and wellness businesses also created and posted their own social teaser videos to further amplify the pop-up. On the actual day, these providers – Color & Curls, Nailed By Daniela, Annie’s Acrylics, and Lilac Tatto Studio – pampered pet owners with intricate temporary hair, nail and tattoo art inspired by portraits of attendees’ pets. No matter how specific or unique the portrait (in one case, an attendee got a tattoo of their pet tarantula), these four beauty providers delivered – and all appointment slots, powered by Booksy, were fully booked leading up to the event. The pet-themed pop-up was decked out in all things pets and also featured a custom pet portrait coffee cart that printed pet-inspired art right on top of lattes. “We handled everything from space design to artist sourcing to building out a fully operational salon space, staffed with professional tattoo, hair, and nail artists in a very short amount of time. Every detail — from the waiting area to the artwork on the wall — was built around a single emotional hook: people's love for their pets,” said Chad Harris, Senior Producer at Humanaut. “To bring this concept to life we decided to focus on a single super specific theme for our talented providers to bring to life: pet portraits. Dallas’ love for pets is as big as everything else in Texas, so we wanted to give pet owners a fun way to express their love,” said Bethany Maxfield, Executive Creative Director at Humanaut. The pop-up builds on a larger-than-life, guerrilla marketing-inspired billboard stunt that Humanaut created for Booksy as a part of its launch in Dallas earlier this summer. Humanaut is an independent creative and production company based in Chattanooga. This  professional campaign titled 'Dallas Beauty Pros Bring Pet Portraits to Life at Sit. Stay. Style.' was published in United States in August, 2026. It was created for the brand: BOOKSY, by ad agency: Humanaut. description: Quilter, the wealth management company, has partnered with independent creative agency Joint to bring its 'Money Needs a Plan' platform to television for the first time, marking a major new chapter for the campaign and the brand's biggest push yet. Developed by Joint, the campaign encourages people to think differently about their money and whether it's simply sitting doing nothing for them. Working in a category often associated with inertia, Joint set out to create a campaign that would feel simple, relatable and relevant to everyday life. Rather than leaning into fear or financial complexity, the creative uses humour to completely reframe people's relationship with money. The campaign marks Quilter's first-ever TV advertising campaign and its biggest brand investment to date. Running for five weeks across TV, BVOD, social and digital channels, the hero film is directed by Tim Godsall, whose acclaimed comedic storytelling brings warmth and relatability to the campaign's central message. Media planning and buying has been led by Bountiful Cow, whose strategy combines the broad reach and emotional impact of premium broadcast television with precision audience targeting to ensure Quilter reaches affluent consumers in trusted, high-attention environments. Launching across Sky, Channel 4 and broadcaster video-on-demand, the campaign uses ONS postcode data to focus activity in affluent areas nationwide, while premium programming including The House of Dragon, Rob & Romesh Vs, Formula 1 Highlights and live Premier League football, Formula 1 and cricket was carefully selected to place Quilter's message alongside content that resonates with its audience. Beyond linear TV, the strategy extends Quilter's storytelling through 40-second VOD creative across ITVX, Amazon and Channel 4, giving the brand more time to build understanding while retaining the premium context, targeting and addressability of broadcaster platforms. By combining broad reach with richer storytelling in trusted viewing environments, the campaign creates a Relative Advantage that helps Quilter stand apart in a category where trust and consideration are critical. Alongside AV, Quilter will bring the campaign to life with new digital executions shot by James Day. The campaign also extends across Meta, LinkedIn and Reddit, with each platform playing a distinct role within the customer journey. Reddit, in particular, enables Quilter to engage financially engaged communities actively researching, discussing and seeking advice on major financial decisions, allowing the brand to participate in relevant conversations at moments of genuine consideration rather than interruption. Jo Harris, chief customer officer at Quilter said, “Most people have things they want to achieve in life, whether that's buying a home, supporting their family, retiring comfortably or simply feeling more in control of their finances. But those goals can be much harder to reach without a plan.” “This campaign is all about helping people see that financial planning doesn't have to be complicated or only for the wealthy. It's about having a clear idea of where you want to get to and taking practical steps to move in the right direction.” “By taking Money Needs a Plan to TV for the first time, we will reach more people with a simple message that whatever matters to you in life, having a plan for your money can help you get there.” Algy Sharman, chief creative officer at Joint added, "It has been so rewarding to see how this brand platform can extend into other channels, including some fantastic new digital and experiential work as well as Quilter's first ever TV spot. It is smart, funny but most importantly persuasive." George MacKean, Business Director at Bountiful Cow, said: “Quilter's first TV campaign required a media strategy that balanced broad reach with smart audience targeting. Premium broadcast delivers the scale, trust and emotional impact needed to introduce the brand to a wider audience, while our digital strategy allows us to continue that conversation in environments where people are actively thinking about their financial future. "Rather than relying solely on demographic targeting, we focused on reaching people in the right contexts and mindsets. Reddit gives Quilter a Relative Advantage because it's still an underutilised platform for financial services brands, allowing Quilter to directly engage communities in moments of genuine consideration instead of competing for attention in crowded channels. It’s an approach that ensures Quilter isn't just reaching the right audience but reaching them when they're most receptive to thinking differently about their money." This  professional campaign titled 'Money Needs a Plan' was published in United Kingdom in July, 2026. It was created for the brand: Quilter, by ad agencies: Bountiful Cow and Joint. description: Monzo has launched ‘Get busy living’, its first global brand platform, as the bank looks to build on its growth across the UK and Europe. The campaign focuses on the idea that when managing money becomes effortless, people have more time to focus on the things they enjoy. It reflects Monzo’s evolution from a fintech challenger into a mainstream bank serving more than 15 million customers and businesses, with services spanning budgeting, saving, borrowing, investing, mortgages and retirement planning. Developed by BBH London with Monzo’s in-house creative studio and NUSA STUDIOS, the campaign is Monzo’s biggest integrated brand campaign to date. Directed by Daniel Wolfe, it features 10 cinematic single-shot films depicting everyday moments, from making a daughter laugh at bathtime to singing in the driver’s seat of a van. Monzo’s products appear subtly within each story, showing how features such as Salary Sorter, Joint Accounts and Monzo for Under 16s can handle financial tasks in the background while customers focus on life. Narrated by Olivia Colman and soundtracked by tracks including ‘Teenage Dirtbag’, ‘Careless Whisper’, ‘Baba O’Riley’ and ‘Days Like This’, the campaign combines warmth, humour and optimism to reinforce Monzo’s broader mission of making money work for everyone. The platform spans TV, cinema, SVOD, BVOD, radio, social, digital and out-of-home, with media planning by Starcom. The OOH campaign includes major placements at Waterloo Motion and Piccadilly Lights, featuring photography by Elliot James Kennedy. This  professional campaign titled 'Get busy living' was published in United Kingdom in August, 2026. It was created for the brand: Monzo, by ad agency: BBH London. description: AB InBev has launched ‘Cheers to Beer’, a new global campaign created with Wieden+Kennedy ahead of International Beer Day on August 7. The campaign celebrates the role beer has played in bringing people together across cultures and generations, highlighting the everyday occasions where a simple cheers can represent celebration, comfort, gratitude, encouragement or connection. The campaign is anchored by a global film that showcases a wide range of moments where beer acts as a catalyst for community and belonging. Building on AB InBev’s 2021 ‘Let’s Grab a Beer’ campaign, the new work focuses on what beer can represent once people come together, from intimate everyday gatherings to major sporting events. The campaign is supported by research from Ipsos and IWSR showing beer’s continued strength among legal-drinking-age consumers, as well as growing interest in moderation and no-alcohol options. The launch follows AB InBev’s Q2 2026 results, which showed continued growth across its beer portfolio. Beer revenue increased 5.6%, while beer volume grew 1.1%, with no-alcohol beer up 27%, Beyond Beer up 44% and its Balanced Choices portfolio up 13%. Together, the campaign and results position beer as a category that continues to adapt to changing consumer preferences while maintaining its longstanding role in social connection. This  professional campaign titled 'Cheers to Beer' was published in United States in August, 2026. It was created for the brand: ABInBev, by ad agency: Wieden+Kennedy NY. video_title: Weight Watchers — Here At Every Point’
description: Weight Watchers has launched ‘Here At Every Point’, a 60-second film directed by Martina Magorin of Golden LA that takes a more personal approach to the weight loss category. Created with Anomaly, the film follows a woman who, between work and motherhood, has gradually lost touch with an earlier version of herself. When she discovers a favourite pair of jeans and an old Polaroid, she begins reflecting on her journey through false starts, small victories and early-morning weigh-ins. The campaign is designed to speak to the growing GLP-1 landscape while positioning Weight Watchers as a broader support system that combines nutrition, coaching, medication and community. Rather than focusing solely on physical transformation, the film centres on accountability, connection and helping people rediscover confidence in their everyday lives. Magorin describes it as a story about finding your way back to the version of yourself that feels comfortable enough to say yes and fully enjoy life. Magorin and director of photography Sean Conaty used an intimate visual approach, relying on eye-level framing, simple locked-off shots and gentle handheld camera work to keep the focus on the character and performance. The wardrobe also evolves throughout the story, moving from layers and softer shapes that help the character hide towards more colourful and intentional clothing that reflects her growing confidence. ‘Here At Every Point’ is rolling out nationally across broadcast, digital and social platforms. This  professional campaign titled 'Here At Every Point’' was published in United States in August, 2026. It was created for the brand: Weight Watchers, by ad agency: Anomaly. description: Built around the universal habit of pressing an almost-finished bar of soap onto a new one, the campaign transforms a familiar household ritual into its central idea. Rather than focusing on product benefits or beauty claims, it celebrates the behaviour itself, using the relationship between old and new soap bars as a playful metaphor for staying connected and making the most of what remains. The film follows this simple but relatable insight through a light-hearted narrative, turning an everyday act of thrift and practicality into an emotional story. By elevating a behaviour that millions of people recognise, the campaign finds meaning in a small domestic habit that is rarely acknowledged in advertising. The story culminates in a memorable visual of leftover soap fragments fused to a fresh bar, reframing what is often considered waste as something valuable. In doing so, the campaign highlights themes of continuity, resourcefulness and everyday ingenuity, celebrating the simple ways people maximize every last bit of a product. This  professional campaign titled ' Almost-Gone Soap' was published in Thailand in May, 2026. It was created for the brand: IngOn Herbal Soap, by ad agency: Wolf BKK. why_ko: 다 써가는 작은 비누 조각을 새 비누에 붙여 쓰는 유니버설한 일상 습관을 서사의 핵심 메카니즘으로 포착한 인사이트 중심의 태국 광고다. 하찮은 생활 속 행위를 사람과 사람 사이의 연결과 연속성에 대한 유쾌한 메타포로 확장하는 연출 기법이 탁월하다. 사소한 소비자 행동 디테일 하나만을 극대화해 감동과 재치를 동시에 만들어내는 기획 프레임을 훔쳐올 만하다.

description: Commissioned by UN Women, Bystander is a tense, intimate short film exploring the split second where instinct, fear and responsibility collide. Across a series of everyday settings - a bus stop late at night, a locker room after a match, an online gaming session, an open-plan office - we witness subtle but recognisable moments of harassment and boundary-crossing behaviour directed towards women. Nothing heightened. Nothing dramatised beyond reality. Just the familiar discomfort of something not quite right. Each character faces the same internal question: intervene, or stay silent? Told through restrained performances, tightening frames and immersive sound design, the film places the audience inside the pause before action, where rationalisation and conscience wrestle for control. Rather than judging its characters, Bystander examines the psychology of inaction in the face of harassment and abuse towards women and the quiet realisation that silence, too, has consequences. This  professional campaign titled 'BYSTANDER' was published in United Kingdom in August, 2026. It was created for the brand: UN Women UK, by ad agency: Media Trust. This Film medium campaign is related to the Education and Public Interest industries and contains 1 media asset. It was submitted 7 days ago.
why_ko: 방관의 순간에 발생하는 내면의 주저함과 갈등을 시각적·음향적 장치로 극대화한 연출법을 참고할 만합니다. 프레임이 점점 좁아지는 구도 변화와 몰입감 있는 사운드 디자인을 결합해 행동 직전의 정적 상태를 심리적 압박감으로 전달합니다. 지극히 일상적인 상황 속 현실적인 기류를 화면 조이기 기법으로 시각화하는 메커니즘이 탁월합니다.

video_title: BBC — What has the BBC ever done for me?
description: Did you spot all these cameos in 'What has the BBC ever done for me?' A skeptical viewer questions the value of the BBC, leading to a journey through iconic shows, programs, and radio services. This fast-paced exploration highlights the breadth of BBC content, from news and drama to nature documentaries and entertainment, while examining the corporation's overall impact on British culture and the economy. Romesh Ranganathan is asking the big question, ‘What has the BBC ever done for me?’ He begins by asking a star-studded Queen Vic pub, complete with Coldplay’s Chris Martin on piano. Romesh travels through Albert Square, Casualty, BBC News, Radio 1Xtra, Graham Norton’s studio, Wimbledon, ending up on stage in Strictly Come Dancing. Along the way he meets Claudia Winkleman and some Traitors, Alan Carr, Daleks, Ruth Jones as Gavin & Stacey’s Nessa, Hey Duggee and Anton Du Beke. There is a BBC for each of us, funded by all of us. description: Confused.com and Leo UK are bringing some of the nation’s most familiar sayings to life in a new campaign capturing the disproportionately good feeling of having Just Used Confused.com. ‘Feels like…’ is the latest chapter of the award-winning brand platform, which celebrates the fleeting sense of triumph that comes from conquering life admin, saving some money and feeling, briefly, like a fully functioning adult. The 2025 instalment of the platform won multiple Golds at Creative Circle and British Arrows, including the prestigious John Webster Award. Each film begins in the real world as someone finishes sorting their insurance with Confused.com. Their relief triggers a comedic cutaway into a heightened world where the feeling is expressed through a familiar idiom, interpreted very literally by a cast of handcrafted animal puppets. The environments and supporting characters were developed and enhanced with AI production tools. In ‘The Cat That Got the Cream’, a man sorting his car insurance cuts to an ageing, bespectacled cat in a supermarket. After seriously considering whether he deserves a pot of cream, the cat drops it into his basket and reasons: “Cream, double cream! That’s coming home with me that, Meow.” ‘Laughing ’til the Cow Comes Home’ introduces Pig and Sheep, two laid-back former university housemates enjoying an afternoon of doing very little while Cow is at his nine-to-five. Pig is midway through a joke when Cow appears in the doorway, briefcase in hand, and shouts: “Oh please don’t stop on my account...” Completing the trio is ‘The Early Bird That Got the Worm’, starring a polished and profoundly pleased-with-herself blue tit. Carrying a shopping bag emblazoned with a worm, she struts past a queue of less fortunate birds and announces: “you should’ve set your alarms”. The characters were developed with BlinkInk stop motion directing duo, Andy Biddle and Adeena Grubb, with every detail designed to build their personalities, from the cat’s increasingly necessary reading glasses to Cow’s carefully pressed workwear, and the early bird’s jumper draped deliberately over her shoulders. Biddle was a lead animator on Wes Anderson’s Fantastic Mr. Fox and Isle of Dogs, while Grubb is a multi-award-winning puppet maker and animation director. Their combined experience in handcrafted filmmaking helped bring the campaign’s familiar idioms to life through characters packed with charm, wit and sharply observed detail. Each film ends with the line, “Insurance feels better when you’ve just used Confused.com”, followed by the familiar Confused.com whistle, performed by its respective puppet character. First introduced with the launch of the ‘Just Used Confused.com’ platform, the whistle has since grown into an established sonic asset for the brand. The campaign will be supported by ten and six second edits, alongside radio and social activity, and will run across TV, BVOD, social and radio in the UK from 7th August. The campaign was developed with Zenith, which led media planning and buying. Together, the team delivered an integrated campaign with an effective media mix, designed to elevate the Just Use Confused.com platform and build fame nationwide. It’s almost impossible to pick a favourite, but Angry Cow has to take the top spot. He was inspired by Mark from Peep Show, while the pig took plenty of cues from Jeremy. We even snuck in Mark’s iconic creamy elephant sofa and named the characters Mark Cowigan, Jeremy UsPork and Super Lamb. If you’re familiar with Peep Show, you’ll understand why. If you’re not… go and watch Peep Show. This  professional campaign titled 'Feels like…' was published in United Kingdom in August, 2026. It was created for the brand: Confused.com, by ad agency: Leo UK. This Film and Integrated media campaign is related to the Insurance industry and contains 3 media assets. description: Cornett Launches ‘Bluegrass Bathing’ for Lexington Tourism VisitLEX invites visitors to for a “grounding” wellness experience they can only get in Lexington, KY on the “best ground in the world” Wellness seekers are spending thousands on retreats, cold plunges, and longevity supplements. Lexington, Kentucky has a simpler suggestion: touch grass. Specifically, Bluegrass. In collaboration with long-time partner Cornett, VisitLEX, the Lexington Convention and Visitors Bureau, today launches Bluegrass Bathing, a new destination-wide wellness experience that invites locals and visitors to kick off their shoes, settle into Lexington's iconic Bluegrass landscape and reconnect with nature. The concept draws inspiration from the growing popularity of “grounding,” also known as “earthing,” a wellness practice centered on making direct contact with the Earth's surface, allowing the body to absorb its natural electrical charge. According to recent medical reports, this connection can help improve sleep, lower stress levels, and reduce inflammation. “You can sit on the ground anywhere. But there’s something special about sitting on the same earth that nourishes the world’s best Thoroughbreds,” said Jonathon Spalding, Group Creative Director at Cornett. “Why touch regular boring grass when you can touch Bluegrass?” As the Horse Capital of the World, visitors are surrounded by more than 450 horse farms. Set among the rolling hills and lush green spaces that define Kentucky's Bluegrass Region, Bluegrass Bathing transforms one of Lexington's most recognizable natural assets into an immersive wellness experience. "If grounding is all about reconnecting with the Earth, then we're inviting folks to start their wellness journey with the best, most natural and nutrient-rich ground in America," said Mary Quinn Ramer, President of VisitLEX. "For centuries, these rolling hills have nurtured some of the world's most celebrated Thoroughbreds and the limestone water that runs beneath it has become the bedrock of our bourbon industry. But it’s also the way this Bluegrass makes you feel. Visitors consistently report they feel more relaxed the moment they touch down in Lexington. Bluegrass Bathing is our invitation to slow down, take a breath and experience the landscape that makes Lexington unlike anywhere else in the world." Visitors can “Bluegrass Bathe” at some of Lexington’s most iconic outdoor spaces, including a selection of Visit Horse Country farms and a handful of Lexington’s scenic parks (including Kentucky Horse Park, Gatton Park, and designated Parks & Rec locations). By booking at participating locations, guests will receive access to a series of curated wellness experiences including Pilates and sound baths along with a selection of guided meditations designed specifically for the program. Additionally, guests can deepen their connection to the Bluegrass by booking a dedicated tour of their host farm after the bathing experience. Each of the guided meditations was inspired by the natural elements that shape Lexington's landscape, encouraging participants to slow down, engage their senses and connect with their surroundings. VisitLEX has also produced a guided Sound Bath video set amidst a local horse farm and led by Amy Hudson, a certified Reiki master and sound healer from the Sound Healing Center of Lexington. To celebrate the launch, VisitLEX has also released a promotional video inspired by luxury wellness retreats. The video follows a solitary Bluegrass Bather enjoying a lush field of Bluegrass while a soothing narrator extols the virtues of one of Kentucky's most abundant natural resources. "We love creating experiences that could only happen in Lexington," added Ramer. "Bluegrass Bathing playfully reminds travelers that sometimes the best reset is simply being present and reconnecting our bodies with the Earth in a beautiful, natural setting. It's wellness, Kentucky-style." Visitors can learn more about Bluegrass Bathing at VisitLEX.com/Bluegrass-Bathing, where they can access all of the guided meditations, explore participating locations and discover additional wellness experiences throughout the destination. video_title: American Pecan Promotion Board — “Surprisingly Snackable Pecans”
description: The American Pecan Promotion Board (APPB) is bringing back its “Surprisingly Snackable Pecans” campaign for a third round, once again teaming with ad agency Signal Theory and creative studio SixTwentySix. The new spots keep the campaign’s signature comedy going, highlighting the everyday moments when pecans are the right call. The third installment of “Surprisingly Snackable Pecans” features three spots built around everyday moments when a pecan snack becomes essential: “Move In”: A father drops his daughter off at college for an emotional goodbye, both wishing Mom could be there. She is, as it turns out, in the car the whole time snacking on pecans. “Drop Off”: A mother tries to get her son to school on time, only to be stopped by a crossing guard who takes pecan snacking very seriously. “Snack Break” (to debut later in 2026): A group of office coworkers speculate about a colleague’s frequent trips outside, unaware she is sneaking away for a pecan fix. “This year we pushed the snack break to feel less casual and a lot more urgent. It’s that moment when you need a snack before you break, and we’ve all been there,” said Joe Wilper, executive creative director at Signal Theory. “The spots lean fully into pecans as the healthy escape you needed at exactly the right moment. Whether it’s the long wait at school pickup, college move-in day or the excuse to finally get up from your desk, we’re reminding people that reaching for pecans is the smart snack in surprising moments.” The new spots mark the third collaboration between Signal Theory and SixTwentySix, led by director Evan Bourque. The partnership has grown tighter with each round, with Signal Theory crediting close creative alignment between both teams for keeping production efficient and the work sharp. "Our goal with these spots was to make them feel like snippets from a movie rather than a commercial, so every choice, from casting to locations to lighting, was built around that idea," said Evan Bourque, director at SixTwentySix. "It's always a pleasure working with the creatives at Signal Theory. They write fun scripts and stay open to new ideas, which makes the end result stronger. The characters are really what make these spots stand out, a quirky character paired with a grounded one, keeping things entertaining." This  professional campaign titled '“Surprisingly Snackable Pecans”' was published in United States in August, 2026. It was created for the brand: American Pecan Promotion Board, by ad agency: Signal Theory. This Digital and Film media campaign is related to the Food industry and contains 2 media assets. description: Canva has launched its first large-scale brand campaign in Thailand, ‘Anyone Can with Canva’, positioning AI-powered video editing as an accessible tool for everyday creativity rather than a skill reserved for professional filmmakers or agencies. Created in partnership with acclaimed Thai filmmaker Nawapol Thamrongrattanarit, the campaign reflects the growing influence of short-form video across Southeast Asia and encourages a wider range of people to participate in visual storytelling. The hero film takes place inside a chaotic advertising agency struggling through endless client revisions before an unlikely group of editors, including a delivery rider, security guard and cleaner, step in to transform the project using Canva’s video editing tools. With its humorous and distinctly local tone, the campaign embraces the idea that creativity can come from anyone, regardless of professional experience, and highlights how technology is lowering barriers to content creation. A key element of the initiative is giving the public access to licensed footage from Thamrongrattanarit’s personal archive, allowing users to experiment with professional-quality material using Canva’s AI-powered editing tools and templates. The campaign also supports Canva’s broader growth strategy in Thailand, where the company has expanded its presence through partnerships such as its education initiative with the Office of the Basic Education Commission, helping bring Canva for Education to millions of students and teachers across the country. This  professional campaign titled 'Anyone Can' was published in Thailand in June, 2026. It was created for the brand: Canva Thailand, by ad agency: Wolf BKK. description: Wolf BKK has partnered with Pruksa to launch an unconventional campaign for the property developer’s new premium residences by presenting a home as if it were the world’s most valuable gadget. Priced at 25 million baht, the campaign taps into society’s fascination with new technology, suggesting that the greatest innovation in improving everyday life may not be a device at all, but a thoughtfully designed home. The campaign began by teasing a mysterious premium gadget through billboards, digital screens, social media and online films, promoting it as a breakthrough invention with life-changing capabilities. As curiosity grew, audiences speculated that the product could be an advanced AI system or another futuristic technology capable of justifying its multimillion-baht price tag. The final reveal showed that the advertised features had never belonged to a gadget, but were the everyday benefits of a home. By disguising a premium residence as a piece of cutting-edge technology, Pruksa reframed its property launch as a conversation about value, challenging people’s obsession with the latest innovations while reminding them that a home remains one of the most meaningful investments in making life easier, smarter and more comfortable. This  professional campaign titled 'The Most Valuable Gadget in the World' was published in Thailand in July, 2026. It was created for the brand: Pruksa, by ad agency: Wolf BKK. description: Today, The Coca‑Cola Company announces the launch of ‘Fizz or Sizz’, a playful, insight‑led campaign that transforms a familiar sensory moment into a mass participation experience. Set in Japan, where fried chicken is hugely popular but not instinctively paired with Coca‑Cola, the campaign is built around a simple but surprising truth: the sound of Coca‑Cola fizzing is almost indistinguishable from the sound of karaage sizzling. By making sound the creative hero, ‘Fizz or Sizz’ turns this uncanny similarity into a nationwide guessing game — asking people one deceptively simple question: is it sizz or fizz? Rolling out across radio, digital out‑of‑home and social media, the campaign invites audiences to listen and engage in real time. Correct guesses can reward participation with a chance to win a free Coke, daily over the course of the week‑long activation. Rather than delivering a traditional product message, ‘Fizz or Sizz’ uses play, sound and immediacy to draw people into a broader cultural conversation about food, taste and refreshment. By gamifying the fizz of Coca‑Cola and placing it alongside the sizzle of freshly cooked food, the campaign subtly rewires cultural associations — making the two sensations feel inseparable in people’s minds. The activation also demonstrates how mass media can feel participatory at scale. Across radio, outdoor and social channels, audiences are invited to actively take part rather than passively observe, creating a shared moment that feels intuitive, accessible and highly shareable. Tish Condeno, Senior Director, Coca‑Cola Trademark Category, Coca‑Cola Japan said: “Sound has a way of triggering recognition in an instant. ‘Fizz or Sizz’ brings together two familiar noises that often blur together, inviting you to listen closely to the crackle of food and the first response of a drink opening or being poured. The result is a light, interactive moment for Coke lovers rooted in food and refreshment.” ‘Fizz or Sizz’ will run across Japan via radio, OOH, social and in‑store engagement touchpoints. The campaign was developed by WPP Open X, led by Grey, supported by Ogilvy, WPP Production, and WPP Media. This  professional campaign titled 'Fizz or Sizz' was published in Japan in April, 2026. It was created for the brand: Coca-Cola, by ad agency: WPP Open X, led by Grey, supported by Ogilvy, WPP Production, and WPP Media.. This Integrated medium campaign is related to the Drinks (Non Alcoholic) industry and contains 3 media assets. It was submitted 4 months ago.
